1	# Reference lock
2	
3	**Load in Step 1b, for every tier.** Refero's research-first method, adapted to this
4	skill's four-tier gate (`SKILL.md` Step 2): Tier 0 locked · Tier 1 derive · Tier 2
5	reference · Tier 3 invent. The lock is not a Tier-2-only artifact — every tier states
6	one before Step 2 runs, because every tier is a claim about where the direction comes
7	from, and an unstated claim is how Tier 1 gets skipped in favour of invention.
8	
9	| | |
10	|---|---|
11	| **Reads** | The brief, Step 1 pre-flight findings, Step 2 tier evidence (`DESIGN.md`, brand assets, user URL/screenshot, or nothing), the design catalog, 21st.dev for tech/SaaS shots, Refero MCP when configured. |
12	| **Does** | Runs the research loop below, captures references as read images (never from memory), fills the reference-lock block and decision ledger, checks the build against anti-averaging and token/media-role preservation. |
13	| **Writes** | Nothing persisted by default — the lock is stated in-session, out loud, before Step 2 and Step 4. When the system is being locked to a portable file, its fields feed [`design-md.md`](design-md.md). |
14	| **Human checks** | Whether the named primary reference is actually the dominant voice in the build, not a label pasted over an averaged result — the one judgment this file cannot automate. |
15	
16	---
17	
18	## What changes per tier
19	
20	The loop is identical; only what plays the role of "the reference" changes.
21	
22	- **Tier 0 — locked.** Reconstructed, not invented: read `DESIGN.md` and what's
23	  already built from it, and write down what "preserve" means. Primary = the
24	  locked system itself.
25	- **Tier 1 — derive.** Primary = the brand evidence (logo, wordmark, hex, deployed
26	  site, `tailwind.config` colours). Borrowed details may come from competitor or
27	  category references; they extend the language, never re-set it.
28	- **Tier 2 — reference.** Primary = the user-supplied URL or screenshot. Refero's
29	  native case; the fields map straight across.
30	- **Tier 3 — invent.** Primary = the invented world's own bible
31	  ([`invention.md`](invention.md)) — locking against it stops the second component
32	  from drifting into a different invented world than the first.
33	
34	At every tier, a major visual choice with no source in the lock is not shipped.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## A brief is not a build target
39	
40	Refero states the rule this file exists to enforce, in one sentence: *"**A brief is not a
41	build target.** Before implementation, lock either a user-provided visual source, an
42	existing product/design-system target, a selected generated mockup, or an explicit
43	reference-locked direction approved for direct build."*
44	
45	This is the sentence that closes the skip route. When the direction feels obvious and the
46	signature act is being built straight from the brief, the visual target still gets named
47	first — one line saying what this is being built *toward* and what must not drift:
48	
49	```text
50	Build target: [existing UI / user screenshot / URL capture / selected mockup / approved reference lock]
51	What must not drift: [canvas, typography, accent roles, layout, media, density]
52	```
53	
54	If no target exists and the visual direction is material, explore options or get one
55	reference-locked direction approved. A build whose only stated source is the brief is a
56	build with no source at all.
57	
58	## Research loop
59	
60	Six angles, not one query:
61	
62	1. **Broad aesthetic** — the mood in plain language ("warm coastal Nordic hospitality").
63	2. **Domain / category** — what this business actually is.
64	3. **Known brand** — a specific strong player in the segment, named.
65	4. **Register** — the row from `SKILL.md`'s register table this brief lands in.
66	5. **Anti-reference** — one thing this build should *not* look like, sharpening the
67	   boundary the same way a rejected direction does in the lock block below.
68	6. **Cross-domain wildcard** — one reference from *outside* the category, chosen for a
69	   quality rather than a subject. *"A banking app can be inspired by a meditation app's
70	   calm."* Upstream's map:
71	
72	   | This brief's domain | Look at |
73	   |---|---|
74	   | Healthcare | Meditation apps (calm), fitness apps (motivation), journaling (reflection) |
75	   | Finance | Productivity tools (clarity), weather apps (data viz), news apps (hierarchy) |
76	   | Education | Games (engagement), music apps (progression), social apps (community) |
77	   | E-commerce | Editorial sites (storytelling), gallery apps (browsing), travel (discovery) |
78	   | Enterprise | Consumer apps (polish), design tools (power + clarity), docs (wayfinding) |
79	
80	   *"Don't force connections — but don't limit yourself to competitors either."* Competitors
81	   solve the same problem the same way, which is precisely how a category default becomes
82	   invisible. `select.py --wildcard` is the catalogue-side version of this angle.
83	
84	**Quality over quantity: *"5 excellent references beat 20 mediocre ones."*** A wall of
85	screenshots is not research; it is deferred judgment. Curate down before capturing.
86	
87	Then: **capture 3–4 full references as images and read them**, long pages in
88	viewport-sized slices. Memory returns wrong facts — two market-leading pages
89	turned out to *centre* their heroes, and one coloured words inside the headline
90	instead of switching typeface, opposite of what was assumed before the images
91	were opened.
92	
93	**Every captured reference carries two lines, not one:**
94	
95	```text
96	What to take: [the specific element or quality to learn from]
97	What to leave: [what does not apply here]
98	```
99	
100	*"This prevents wholesale copying."* A reference with no lesson is decoration, and a
101	reference with only a "take" line is the one that quietly becomes the whole build. The
102	"leave" line is also what makes the primary/borrowed split below enforceable rather than
103	declarative.
104	
105	**Extract more than colour and type.** From each reference, read out: layout system,
106	section rhythm and composition · card, button and surface treatments · borders, shadows,
107	radius · elevation and depth rules · imagery, graphic and illustration treatment · media
108	asset strategy (real asset, generated, code-native primitive, product screenshot, or
109	placeholder) · do and don't rules · **one memorable visual move to adapt**. A lock that
110	carries a palette and a typeface and nothing structural is why a build "referenced" a page
111	it looks nothing like.
112	
113	**Give each source a bounded job.** *"Primary style: overall mood, density, and structure.
114	Secondary styles: specific borrowed details. User context: adapt everything to the product,
115	audience, and task."* A source with no job is a source that gets averaged.
116	
117	From the 3–4 captured, pick **one primary** and take **1–2 borrowed details** from
118	the rest. Nothing else survives into the lock.
119	
120	**Flag accessibility failures in the references themselves.** *"A beautiful reference with
121	2:1 contrast ratios is not inspiration — it's a cautionary tale."* Name it when you capture
122	it, so the trait does not travel into the lock as craft.
123	
124	### Sources, in order
125	
126	1. **The design catalog** — `~/anti-slop-design/design-catalogue/`,
127	   `python scripts/query.py --family … --register … --grammar …`. Query by the
128	   register named in `SKILL.md`'s table, not by vibe.
129	2. **Inspo MCP** (`mcp__inspo__*`), per [`inspo-mcp.md`](inspo-mcp.md) — the second
130	   source, right after the catalogue, when the catalogue lacks the page's form. The
131	   primary reference's tokens are fetched with `get_design_system`, never read off
132	   an image.
133	3. **User-supplied URL or screenshot** — Tier 2's native input; also valid at any
134	   tier as a borrowed-detail source.
135	4. **21st.dev** for tech/SaaS product shots — browse, screenshot, study the
136	   treatment; borrow the principle and rebuild it in the locked tokens, never paste
137	   a component with its own palette into a Tier 0–2 build.
138	5. **Refero MCP**, if configured — `refero_search_styles` → `refero_get_style`.
139	   Optional. State plainly when it is not configured rather than silently skipping
140	   it; do not treat its absence as license to skip the research loop itself.
141	
142	### When the results are weak
143	
144	Sparse or generic results are a query problem before they are a source problem. Climb this
145	ladder before concluding the catalogue has nothing (Refero `mcp-tools.md` § If Results Are
146	Weak):
147	
148	1. **Broaden the query.**
149	2. **Remove extra adjectives or constraints.** Two adjectives and a register is usually one
150	   adjective too many.
151	3. **Search adjacent categories.**
152	4. **Try a known-product or best-brand query.** Name a specific strong player instead of
153	   describing a type.
154	5. **Inspect later pages.** The first page of any index is the most averaged part of it.
155	
156	Only after all five is "no usable reference in this register" a finding — and then it is
157	stated in the lock, not silently converted into invention.
158	
159	### Transcribe the category's live headlines
160	
161	Before writing a word of copy, read the **five best live pages in the category and quote
162	their headlines verbatim** into the lock. *"The bar is what the reader has already seen, not
163	what sounds nice in isolation"* (`upstream/slopmonster/references/sources.md`). Five lines,
164	copied exactly, with the source named. They belong here rather than in
165	[`copy-gate.md`](copy-gate.md) because they are a *reference* capture: the same discipline
166	as the four screenshots, applied to language, and read before the copy pass rather than
167	during it.
168	
169	## The reference-lock block
170	
171	Verbatim fields, filled before any code:
172	
173	```text
174	Primary reference/direction: [one dominant source, named]
175	Preserve: [3-5 traits that must survive: canvas, type, accent, layout, density, media]
176	Borrow only: [1-2 specific secondary details]
177	Role rules: [source token/component meanings to preserve — CTA-only, code-only, decorative-only]
178	Media strategy: [photo:unsplash | photo:pexels | product surface | drawn system | generated | placeholder]
179	Reject: [defaults/averages that would collapse the direction]
180	Token commitments: [canvas, type, accent, radius, border/shadow, imagery — each with its role]
181	```
182	
183	**Media strategy is an enum, not prose.** Pick exactly one value per media slot so
184	drift is visible at a glance: a hero declared `photo:unsplash` that quietly becomes
185	a CSS gradient is a caught regression; a hero declared "some kind of photo" is not.
186	
187	## Decision ledger
188	
189	Every entry in the lock traces back through this table:
190	
191	| Decision | Source | Source rule/role | Why |
192	|---|---|---|---|
193	| [palette / type / layout / media choice] | [reference / catalog query / brand asset / craft rule] | [token or component role to preserve] | [reason specific to this brief] |
194	| **Memorable detail** | [the reference the move was adapted from] | [what the move does on this page] | [why *this* brief earns it] |
195	
196	**A major visual choice with no row here is not shipped.** Not "shipped and
197	justified after" — the row exists before the choice does.
198	
199	**The `Memorable detail` row is mandatory, and the rule applies to it too.** Refero's
200	requirement is unambiguous: *"Create at least one memorable detail: a visual move,
201	interaction, layout choice, or copy detail users would remember."* No row, not shipped —
202	including for the signature act itself, which is the row most often left blank on the
203	grounds that it is obvious. An example of a filled row from upstream's own worked case:
204	*"Memorable detail | 'Operational value' strip showing saved hours/cost by plan | Brief +
205	analytics product context | Metric strip as evidence, not decoration | Makes pricing feel
206	tied to outcome."*
207	
208	## The asset lock
209	
210	Written **before** anyone starts searching or generating — Step 5b has a pipeline but no
211	spec upstream of it, and an asset sourced without a spec is an asset chosen by whatever the
212	search returned. One block per media slot:
213	
214	```text
215	Asset role: [hero image / texture / illustration / thumbnail / cutout]
216	Slot: [dimensions / aspect ratio / location on the page]
217	Art direction: [source, palette, subject, rendering, crop, density]
218	Avoid: [wrong palette, extra text, brand drift, generic placeholders]
219	```
220	
221	The `Avoid` line is the one that earns its keep: it is the reject field applied to a single
222	asset, and it is what a QA pass compares the delivered frame against.
223	*"Generated assets must be placed into the implementation before handoff or documented as
224	blocked"* — never quietly downgraded to a gradient. That downgrade is the media-role drift
225	this file's next section already bans, caught one step earlier.
226	
227	---
228	
229	## Anti-averaging
230	
231	Choose a dominant direction. Secondary references contribute narrow, named details;
232	they do not get to soften the primary one. The failure mode is specific: a dark
233	workbench reference, an acid-yellow document site, and a serif editorial page do not
234	average into a warm cream canvas with muted clay accents — **dark + acid + serif is
235	not cream + orange + polite serif.** Dark → cream, saturated → muted clay, sharp →
236	rounded, distinctive layout → generic hero-and-sections: each swap is the
237	intersection eating the direction, not synthesis.
238	
239	Run these against the lock before shipping — ported from `anti-ai-slop.md`:
240	
241	- **Identity test.** If the first viewport could belong to any other company,
242	  branding lost to averaging. Add the one detail that makes this unmistakably *this*
243	  brand's build.
244	- **Editorial test.** If swapping the logo for a coffee shop, boutique hotel, or
245	  literary magazine still makes the hero feel plausible, the build has drifted into
246	  generic calm-editorial slop regardless of what the lock says on paper.
247	- **Screenshot test.** Would this pass next to real products in the named
248	  register, or does it read as the safe middle every other page also landed on?
249	
250	A lock that names a dominant primary and still fails these three was averaged during
251	implementation, not during research — check the built page against the lock's
252	"Reject" line specifically.
253	
254	## Token-role and media-role preservation
255	
256	**Token-role preservation.** A source's role for a colour, radius, shadow, or
257	component is part of the token, not separable from it. A CTA-only accent used as a
258	section background, a code-only syntax colour promoted to UI chrome, or a decorative
259	gradient turned into a core surface are all role drift. Preserve the role or drop
260	the token — never repurpose it to make a layout "work."
261	
262	**Media-role preservation.** An image-led reference never collapses to text-only
263	because the image was hard to produce. If the real asset genuinely is not
264	available, the placeholder must be honest, not silent:
265	
266	```text
267	Placeholder — [slot name]
268	Aspect: [ratio, e.g. 16:9 desktop / 4:3 mobile]
269	Art direction: [subject, lighting, crop the real asset will match]
270	Alt: [describes the intended real subject, not "placeholder image"]
271	```
272	
273	A placeholder with no aspect ratio, no art direction, and generic alt text is the
274	same failure as no image at all — it just fails one render cycle later.
275	
276	---
277	
278	## Three persona sketches
279	
280	`SKILL.md` Step 5 pass 12 and [`verbs/review.md`](verbs/review.md) § 4 both resolve ties
281	with "named personas". Nothing in the chain created any, so the tie-break pointed at an
282	artifact that did not exist. It does now, and it is three lines in `BRIEF.md` — not the
283	per-project persona documents upstream files away, which is a research deliverable this
284	chain has no room for.
285	
286	Select and write **three**, following upstream's proportions (*"2–3 primary users, 1–2 edge
287	case users, 1 stress case user"*), compressed to one line each:
288	
289	```text
290	Primary: [who they are] · [device and connection] · [what they came to do]
291	Edge:    [who sits at the margin] · [the ability or context that puts them there] · [what breaks first]
292	Stress:  [the same job under a named difficult circumstance] · [what they cannot afford to lose]
293	```
294	
295	**The conditions are situational, not only permanent.** Upstream's spectrum is explicit that
296	*"bright sunlight, noisy environment, one hand occupied, driving, multitasking, emotional
297	distress, unfamiliar language, slow connection"* belong beside vision, hearing, motor and
298	cognitive conditions. A stress persona on a Swedish harbour-restaurant page is a person on a
299	phone, outdoors, in sun, deciding where to eat in the next ten minutes — and that persona
300	decides more layout questions than any abstract one.
301	
302	**Write the intersections down.** *"A sighted user in bright sunlight has similar needs to a
303	low-vision user. A stressed parent holding a baby has similar motor constraints to someone
304	with limited hand mobility. A non-native speaker has similar needs to someone with a
305	cognitive processing difference."* Each intersection is a universal-design opportunity: one
306	fix that pays twice.
307	
308	**Then ask the one question that makes the set honest:** *"Which persona makes you most
309	uncomfortable?"* — *"that one probably needs the most attention."* Ask it of the brief, and
310	of the user when there is a user to ask. Discomfort is the signal that a persona was
311	included for completeness and is about to be designed around rather than for.
312	
313	Sketches that read as cardboard cutouts have failed. The check is upstream's own: *"do these
314	feel like real people, or cardboard cutouts?"*
315	
316	## Feeding Step 2 and Step 5
317	
318	**Into Step 2.** At **Tier 2**, the lock *is* the direction — its primary reference
319	sets the token commitments directly. At **Tiers 0–1**, the lock is the **quality
320	bar** the locked or derived system has to clear: the locked tokens still win on
321	value, but the captured references are what "as good as" means, concretely.
322	
323	**Into Step 5 visual QA.** Carry the lock's fields straight into the QA pass:
324	
325	```text
326	Source truth: [the reference lock, or the DESIGN.md it fed]
327	Implementation evidence: [local screenshot, deployed URL screenshot, captured app state]
328	Viewport/state: [desktop/mobile, route, theme, interaction state]
329	```
330	
331	Classify findings P0–P3 (broken/unreadable · major drift from the lock · moderate
332	mismatch or missing state · post-handoff polish). **No handoff with an open P0, P1,
333	or P2.** A P3 may ship with the finding named; P0–P2 block.
334	
335	## Worked example — Skärgårdskrogen (Swedish harbour restaurant, warm photographic)
336	
337	A harbourside restaurant on the Bohuslän coast. Register: **warm photographic**
338	(`SKILL.md` register table — harbour restaurant, guesthouse, tourism, family
339	business), with `klova/` as this skill's own in-repo worked example for the
340	register (`house-physics.md`).
341	
342	**Research loop:**
343	
344	1. Broad aesthetic — "warm coastal Nordic hospitality."
345	2. Domain/category — harbourside seafood dining, Bohuslän archipelago.
346	3. Known brand — a west-coast Swedish harbour restaurant with a photograph-led site.
347	4. Register — warm photographic, per the table above; cross-check against `klova/`.
348	5. Anti-reference — the editorial-print register (`calyx.html`): its apparatus on a
349	   family harbour restaurant reads as pretension, not craft.
350	
351	Four captured and read: `klova/` itself, two competitor harbour-restaurant sites,
352	and `calyx.html` as the anti-reference boundary check.
353	
354	**Reference-lock block:**
355	
356	```text
357	Primary reference/direction: klova/ — centred logo lockup over full-bleed harbour photography, no rail, no kicker, no edition marker.
358	Preserve: centred logo lockup with no rail; full-bleed hero photograph with generous framing air on secondary images; one real outlined button sized to be pressed; warm serif display at conversational (not oversized-drop-cap) scale; dark-navy footer as the page's one tonal inversion.
359	Borrow only: dotted carousel indicator for the food gallery (competitor B — klova/ has no gallery, so this is a genuinely new need, not a style import); 12px rounded image corners (competitor B).
360	Role rules: the outlined button is CTA-only, never a secondary link style; the navy footer tone is inversion-only, never a section background elsewhere on the page.
361	Media strategy: photo:unsplash, sourced and vendored per photo-sources.md until real restaurant photography is supplied; hero 16:9 desktop / 4:3 mobile, framed with 24-48px air — never full-bleed-with-type-over, the editorial-print move this build explicitly rejects.
362	Reject: kicker microformat, grain film, ledger pricing, edition markers, italic serif drop caps — all editorial-print apparatus a family harbour restaurant cannot plausibly publish.
363	Token commitments: warm ivory canvas; near-black ink; one terracotta accent used only on the button and one wordmark word (never as fill); slate captions with a separate, measured value for the dark footer ground.
364	```
365	
366	**Decision ledger:**
367	
368	| Decision | Source | Source rule/role | Why |
369	|---|---|---|---|
370	| Warm photographic, not editorial print | `SKILL.md` register table + anti-reference read of `calyx.html` | register selects apparatus | Family-run harbour restaurant, not a publishing entity |
371	| Centred logo lockup, no rail | `klova/` (primary) | layout role: identity-first hero | The photograph is the primary hire, not editorial structure |
372	| Real outlined button | `klova/` (primary) | CTA-only | Warm-photographic register expects a pressable button, unlike print/cinematic typeset links |
373	| Dotted carousel for gallery | Competitor B (borrowed) | gallery navigation only | `klova/` had no gallery; licensed as one named borrowed detail, not a wholesale style import |
374	| One terracotta accent, display-scale only | `house-physics.md` structural rule | accent role: CTA + display, never fill | Prevents the accent diluting into a second colour system |
375	
376	A rejected direction here would average `klova/`'s warm photographic register with
377	`calyx.html`'s editorial apparatus into a soft-cream page with a restrained kicker
378	and a half-outlined button that is neither a typeset link nor a real one — the
379	dark+acid+serif-vs-cream+orange+polite-serif failure, in miniature.
380	
381	## Two additions from the 2026-09-03 A/B run (AB05)
382	
383	- **A colour-swapped word in a headline is a gate-89 signal even without a serif.** "Se *exakt* vad som ändrades" with *exakt* in the accent is the same reflex as the italic word swap; use it only when a locked reference does it and the word carries the claim.
384	- **Token commitments name the anatomy of every priced or listed surface.** Write `pricing: ledger (hairline rows, display numerals)` or `features: label-rail`, so the lock carries house physics into Step 4 instead of falling back to bordered cards.
385

   solve the same problem the same way, which is precisely how a category default becomes
   invisible. `select.py --wildcard` is the catalogue-side version of this angle.

**Quality over quantity: *"5 excellent references beat 20 mediocre ones."*** A wall of
screenshots is not research; it is deferred judgment. Curate down before capturing.

Then: **capture 3–4 full references as images and read them**, long pages in
viewport-sized slices. Memory returns wrong facts — two market-leading pages
turned out to *centre* their heroes, and one coloured words inside the headline
instead of switching typeface, opposite of what was assumed before the images
were opened.

**Every captured reference carries two lines, not one:**

```text
What to take: [the specific element or quality to learn from]
What to leave: [what does not apply here]
```

*"This prevents wholesale copying."* A reference with no lesson is decoration, and a
reference with only a "take" line is the one that quietly becomes the whole build. The
"leave" line is also what makes the primary/borrowed split below enforceable rather than
declarative.

**Extract more than colour and type.** From each reference, read out: layout system,
section rhythm and composition · card, button and surface treatments · borders, shadows,
radius · elevation and depth rules · imagery, graphic and illustration treatment · media
asset strategy (real asset, generated, code-native primitive, product screenshot, or
placeholder) · do and don't rules · **one memorable visual move to adapt**. A lock that
carries a palette and a typeface and nothing structural is why a build "referenced" a page
it looks nothing like.

**Give each source a bounded job.** *"Primary style: overall mood, density, and structure.
Secondary styles: specific borrowed details. User context: adapt everything to the product,
audience, and task."* A source with no job is a source that gets averaged.

From the 3–4 captured, pick **one primary** and take **1–2 borrowed details** from
the rest. Nothing else survives into the lock.

**Flag accessibility failures in the references themselves.** *"A beautiful reference with
2:1 contrast ratios is not inspiration — it's a cautionary tale."* Name it when you capture
it, so the trait does not travel into the lock as craft.

### Sources, in order

1. **The design catalog** — `~/anti-slop-design/design-catalogue/`,
   `python scripts/query.py --family … --register … --grammar …`. Query by the
   register named in `SKILL.md`'s table, not by vibe.
2. **Inspo MCP** (`mcp__inspo__*`), per [`inspo-mcp.md`](inspo-mcp.md) — the second
   source, right after the catalogue, when the catalogue lacks the page's form. The
   primary reference's tokens are fetched with `get_design_system`, never read off
   an image.
3. **User-supplied URL or screenshot** — Tier 2's native input; also valid at any
   tier as a borrowed-detail source.
4. **21st.dev** for tech/SaaS product shots — browse, screenshot, study the
   treatment; borrow the principle and rebuild it in the locked tokens, never paste
   a component with its own palette into a Tier 0–2 build.
5. **Refero MCP**, if configured — `refero_search_styles` → `refero_get_style`.
   Optional. State plainly when it is not configured rather than silently skipping
   it; do not treat its absence as license to skip the research loop itself.

### When the results are weak

Sparse or generic results are a query problem before they are a source problem. Climb this
ladder before concluding the catalogue has nothing (Refero `mcp-tools.md` § If Results Are
Weak):

1. **Broaden the query.**
2. **Remove extra adjectives or constraints.** Two adjectives and a register is usually one
   adjective too many.
3. **Search adjacent categories.**
4. **Try a known-product or best-brand query.** Name a specific strong player instead of
   describing a type.
5. **Inspect later pages.** The first page of any index is the most averaged part of it.

Only after all five is "no usable reference in this register" a finding — and then it is
stated in the lock, not silently converted into invention.

### Transcribe the category's live headlines

Before writing a word of copy, read the **five best live pages in the category and quote
their headlines verbatim** into the lock. *"The bar is what the reader has already seen, not
what sounds nice in isolation"* (`upstream/slopmonster/references/sources.md`). Five lines,
copied exactly, with the source named. They belong here rather than in
[`copy-gate.md`](copy-gate.md) because they are a *reference* capture: the same discipline
as the four screenshots, applied to language, and read before the copy pass rather than
during it.

## The reference-lock block

Verbatim fields, filled before any code:

```text
Primary reference/direction: [one dominant source, named]
Preserve: [3-5 traits that must survive: canvas, type, accent, layout, density, media]
Borrow only: [1-2 specific secondary details]
Role rules: [source token/component meanings to preserve — CTA-only, code-only, decorative-only]
Media strategy: [photo:unsplash | photo:pexels | product surface | drawn system | generated | placeholder]
Reject: [defaults/averages that would collapse the direction]
Token commitments: [canvas, type, accent, radius, border/shadow, imagery — each with its role]
```

**Media strategy is an enum, not prose.** Pick exactly one value per media slot so
drift is visible at a glance: a hero declared `photo:unsplash` that quietly becomes
a CSS gradient is a caught regression; a hero declared "some kind of photo" is not.

## Decision ledger

Every entry in the lock traces back through this table:

| Decision | Source | Source rule/role | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| [palette / type / layout / media choice] | [reference / catalog query / brand asset / craft rule] | [token or component role to preserve] | [reason specific to this brief] |
| **Memorable detail** | [the reference the move was adapted from] | [what the move does on this page] | [why *this* brief earns it] |

**A major visual choice with no row here is not shipped.** Not "shipped and
justified after" — the row exists before the choice does.

**The `Memorable detail` row is mandatory, and the rule applies to it too.** Refero's
requirement is unambiguous: *"Create at least one memorable detail: a visual move,
interaction, layout choice, or copy detail users would remember."* No row, not shipped —
including for the signature act itself, which is the row most often left blank on the
grounds that it is obvious. An example of a filled row from upstream's own worked case:
*"Memorable detail | 'Operational value' strip showing saved hours/cost by plan | Brief +
analytics product context | Metric strip as evidence, not decoration | Makes pricing feel
tied to outcome."*

## The asset lock

Written **before** anyone starts searching or generating — Step 5b has a pipeline but no
spec upstream of it, and an asset sourced without a spec is an asset chosen by whatever the
search returned. One block per media slot:

```text
Asset role: [hero image / texture / illustration / thumbnail / cutout]
Slot: [dimensions / aspect ratio / location on the page]
Art direction: [source, palette, subject, rendering, crop, density]
Avoid: [wrong palette, extra text, brand drift, generic placeholders]
```

The `Avoid` line is the one that earns its keep: it is the reject field applied to a single
asset, and it is what a QA pass compares the delivered frame against.
*"Generated assets must be placed into the implementation before handoff or documented as
blocked"* — never quietly downgraded to a gradient. That downgrade is the media-role drift
this file's next section already bans, caught one step earlier.

---

## Anti-averaging

Choose a dominant direction. Secondary references contribute narrow, named details;
they do not get to soften the primary one. The failure mode is specific: a dark
workbench reference, an acid-yellow document site, and a serif editorial page do not
average into a warm cream canvas with muted clay accents — **dark + acid + serif is
not cream + orange + polite serif.** Dark → cream, saturated → muted clay, sharp →
rounded, distinctive layout → generic hero-and-sections: each swap is the
intersection eating the direction, not synthesis.

Run these against the lock before shipping — ported from `anti-ai-slop.md`:

- **Identity test.** If the first viewport could belong to any other company,
  branding lost to averaging. Add the one detail that makes this unmistakably *this*
  brand's build.
- **Editorial test.** If swapping the logo for a coffee shop, boutique hotel, or
  literary magazine still makes the hero feel plausible, the build has drifted into
  generic calm-editorial slop regardless of what the lock says on paper.
- **Screenshot test.** Would this pass next to real products in the named
  register, or does it read as the safe middle every other page also landed on?

A lock that names a dominant primary and still fails these three was averaged during
implementation, not during research — check the built page against the lock's
"Reject" line specifically.

## Token-role and media-role preservation

**Token-role preservation.** A source's role for a colour, radius, shadow, or
component is part of the token, not separable from it. A CTA-only accent used as a
section background, a code-only syntax colour promoted to UI chrome, or a decorative
gradient turned into a core surface are all role drift. Preserve the role or drop
the token — never repurpose it to make a layout "work."

**Media-role preservation.** An image-led reference never collapses to text-only
because the image was hard to produce. If the real asset genuinely is not
available, the placeholder must be honest, not silent:

```text
Placeholder — [slot name]
Aspect: [ratio, e.g. 16:9 desktop / 4:3 mobile]
Art direction: [subject, lighting, crop the real asset will match]
Alt: [describes the intended real subject, not "placeholder image"]
```

A placeholder with no aspect ratio, no art direction, and generic alt text is the
same failure as no image at all — it just fails one render cycle later.

---

## Three persona sketches

`SKILL.md` Step 5 pass 12 and [`verbs/review.md`](verbs/review.md) § 4 both resolve ties
with "named personas". Nothing in the chain created any, so the tie-break pointed at an
artifact that did not exist. It does now, and it is three lines in `BRIEF.md` — not the
per-project persona documents upstream files away, which is a research deliverable this
chain has no room for.

Select and write **three**, following upstream's proportions (*"2–3 primary users, 1–2 edge
case users, 1 stress case user"*), compressed to one line each:

```text
Primary: [who they are] · [device and connection] · [what they came to do]
Edge:    [who sits at the margin] · [the ability or context that puts them there] · [what breaks first]
Stress:  [the same job under a named difficult circumstance] · [what they cannot afford to lose]
```

**The conditions are situational, not only permanent.** Upstream's spectrum is explicit that
*"bright sunlight, noisy environment, one hand occupied, driving, multitasking, emotional
distress, unfamiliar language, slow connection"* belong beside vision, hearing, motor and
cognitive conditions. A stress persona on a Swedish harbour-restaurant page is a person on a
phone, outdoors, in sun, deciding where to eat in the next ten minutes — and that persona
decides more layout questions than any abstract one.

**Write the intersections down.** *"A sighted user in bright sunlight has similar needs to a
low-vision user. A stressed parent holding a baby has similar motor constraints to someone
with limited hand mobility. A non-native speaker has similar needs to someone with a
cognitive processing difference."* Each intersection is a universal-design opportunity: one
fix that pays twice.

**Then ask the one question that makes the set honest:** *"Which persona makes you most
uncomfortable?"* — *"that one probably needs the most attention."* Ask it of the brief, and
of the user when there is a user to ask. Discomfort is the signal that a persona was
included for completeness and is about to be designed around rather than for.

Sketches that read as cardboard cutouts have failed. The check is upstream's own: *"do these
feel like real people, or cardboard cutouts?"*

## Feeding Step 2 and Step 5

**Into Step 2.** At **Tier 2**, the lock *is* the direction — its primary reference
sets the token commitments directly. At **Tiers 0–1**, the lock is the **quality
bar** the locked or derived system has to clear: the locked tokens still win on
value, but the captured references are what "as good as" means, concretely.

**Into Step 5 visual QA.** Carry the lock's fields straight into the QA pass:

```text
Source truth: [the reference lock, or the DESIGN.md it fed]
Implementation evidence: [local screenshot, deployed URL screenshot, captured app state]
Viewport/state: [desktop/mobile, route, theme, interaction state]
```

Classify findings P0–P3 (broken/unreadable · major drift from the lock · moderate
mismatch or missing state · post-handoff polish). **No handoff with an open P0, P1,
or P2.** A P3 may ship with the finding named; P0–P2 block.

## Worked example — Skärgårdskrogen (Swedish harbour restaurant, warm photographic)

A harbourside restaurant on the Bohuslän coast. Register: **warm photographic**
(`SKILL.md` register table — harbour restaurant, guesthouse, tourism, family
business), with `klova/` as this skill's own in-repo worked example for the
register (`house-physics.md`).

**Research loop:**

1. Broad aesthetic — "warm coastal Nordic hospitality."
2. Domain/category — harbourside seafood dining, Bohuslän archipelago.
3. Known brand — a west-coast Swedish harbour restaurant with a photograph-led site.
4. Register — warm photographic, per the table above; cross-check against `klova/`.
5. Anti-reference — the editorial-print register (`calyx.html`): its apparatus on a
   family harbour restaurant reads as pretension, not craft.

Four captured and read: `klova/` itself, two competitor harbour-restaurant sites,
and `calyx.html` as the anti-reference boundary check.

**Reference-lock block:**

```text
Primary reference/direction: klova/ — centred logo lockup over full-bleed harbour photography, no rail, no kicker, no edition marker.
Preserve: centred logo lockup with no rail; full-bleed hero photograph with generous framing air on secondary images; one real outlined button sized to be pressed; warm serif display at conversational (not oversized-drop-cap) scale; dark-navy footer as the page's one tonal inversion.
Borrow only: dotted carousel indicator for the food gallery (competitor B — klova/ has no gallery, so this is a genuinely new need, not a style import); 12px rounded image corners (competitor B).
Role rules: the outlined button is CTA-only, never a secondary link style; the navy footer tone is inversion-only, never a section background elsewhere on the page.
Media strategy: photo:unsplash, sourced and vendored per photo-sources.md until real restaurant photography is supplied; hero 16:9 desktop / 4:3 mobile, framed with 24-48px air — never full-bleed-with-type-over, the editorial-print move this build explicitly rejects.
Reject: kicker microformat, grain film, ledger pricing, edition markers, italic serif drop caps — all editorial-print apparatus a family harbour restaurant cannot plausibly publish.
Token commitments: warm ivory canvas; near-black ink; one terracotta accent used only on the button and one wordmark word (never as fill); slate captions with a separate, measured value for the dark footer ground.
```

**Decision ledger:**

| Decision | Source | Source rule/role | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Warm photographic, not editorial print | `SKILL.md` register table + anti-reference read of `calyx.html` | register selects apparatus | Family-run harbour restaurant, not a publishing entity |
| Centred logo lockup, no rail | `klova/` (primary) | layout role: identity-first hero | The photograph is the primary hire, not editorial structure |
| Real outlined button | `klova/` (primary) | CTA-only | Warm-photographic register expects a pressable button, unlike print/cinematic typeset links |
| Dotted carousel for gallery | Competitor B (borrowed) | gallery navigation only | `klova/` had no gallery; licensed as one named borrowed detail, not a wholesale style import |
| One terracotta accent, display-scale only | `house-physics.md` structural rule | accent role: CTA + display, never fill | Prevents the accent diluting into a second colour system |

A rejected direction here would average `klova/`'s warm photographic register with
`calyx.html`'s editorial apparatus into a soft-cream page with a restrained kicker
and a half-outlined button that is neither a typeset link nor a real one — the
dark+acid+serif-vs-cream+orange+polite-serif failure, in miniature.

## Two additions from the 2026-09-03 A/B run (AB05)

- **A colour-swapped word in a headline is a gate-89 signal even without a serif.** "Se *exakt* vad som ändrades" with *exakt* in the accent is the same reflex as the italic word swap; use it only when a locked reference does it and the word carries the claim.
- **Token commitments name the anatomy of every priced or listed surface.** Write `pricing: ledger (hairline rows, display numerals)` or `features: label-rail`, so the lock carries house physics into Step 4 instead of falling back to bordered cards.

27	
28	**Every new build animates with GSAP** (+ScrollTrigger, SplitText when text is
29	split) **and Lenis.** Scrollcraft (`scripts/scroll/`) stays only for pages already
30	built on it — do not port an existing scrollcraft page to GSAP+Lenis just because
31	it's the new default. **Never mix the two engines on one page**: two scroll owners
32	is two RAF loops fighting for the same frame. Anton's instruction: GSAP+Lenis for
33	all animations, applied wherever the motion fits the design and elements of each
34	page.
35	
36	Vendored locally from `scripts/motion/vendor/` (gsap 3.15.0, ScrollTrigger,
37	SplitText, lenis 1.3.26 + `lenis.css`) — copy the whole folder into the build's
38	`assets/vendor/`; never a CDN at runtime. GSAP 3.13+ including SplitText is free.
39	
40	The init, verbatim — house deviations from Lenis's own defaults, each explained
41	once here so no builder reads the Lenis README and takes the default instead:
42	
43	```js
44	var lenis = new Lenis({ autoRaf: false, anchors: true, respectReducedMotion: false, lerp: 0.1 });
45	window.__lenis = lenis;
46	gsap.ticker.add(function (time) { lenis.raf(time * 1000); });
47	gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0);
48	lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update);
49	```
50	
51	- **`respectReducedMotion: false`.** Lenis's own default is `true`, which would
52	  silently switch off all motion for Anton, whose Windows runs with animation
53	  effects off (house rule F-011 / CARL design decision 2026-09-07). Rörelse spelar
54	  alltid — motion always plays.
55	- **`anchors: true`.** Lenis's default is `false`, which breaks in-page anchor
56	  links silently — no error, they just stop scrolling to the target.
57	- **`autoRaf: false`, driven by `gsap.ticker`.** `gsap.ticker` is the only RAF
58	  driver on the page; Lenis's own rAF loop would be a second one racing it.
59	- **`gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)`** and **`lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)`**
60	  keep GSAP's tab-blur catch-up off and ScrollTrigger's cached positions synced to
61	  Lenis's virtual scroll on every frame.
62	- **`window.__lenis`** is the dev hook every jump-test drives:
63	  `lenis.scrollTo(el, {immediate:true})`, never `window.scrollTo`.
64	
65	No `scrollerProxy` (Lenis scrolls the real page, not a virtual container). No CSS
66	`scroll-behavior: smooth` anywhere — it fights Lenis's own smoothing.

68	**Iframes.** `lenis.css` sets `pointer-events: none` on iframes while smooth-scroll

110	## The cue contract — what verification actually catches you on
111	
112	`data-sc-cue="from [to [rampIn [rampOut]]]"`, all in act progress 0–1.
113	
114	| Form | Behaviour |
115	|---|---|
116	| `"0.2"` | fades in at 0.2, **holds to the end of the act** |
117	| `"0.1 0.6"` | in, plateau, out (ramps default 30% of window each) |
118	| `"0 0.78 0"` | **greet**: full opacity at act start, then fades — the hero form |
119	| `"0 1 0 0"` | **greet and hold**: full at p=0, no ramp either end |
120	
121	**The plateau is the point.** Without one, a cue is a triangle that touches full
122	opacity for a single instant, so the reader has to stop on exactly the right
123	pixel to see the line at full strength and every heading reads slightly faded.
124	`"0.1 0.9 0.15 0.4"` — fast in, long slow out — is the confident form. Cue
125	windows on a pinned act **overlap by design**, roughly 15% of the act: the
126	outgoing line is still fading while the next arrives, and a gap between cues
127	reads as a loading failure.
128	
129	Five rules, each one a real bug this fixture has caught:
130	
131	- **A hero cue needs the greet form.** A plain `"0 0.7"` means the first
132	  screen every visitor sees has no headline on it.
133	- **The last act's cue must hold** (one value). A two-value close cue fades
134	  the CTA out before the page ends.
135	- **Only the last act may hold.** A one-value cue on a *middle* pinned act
136	  stays lit through the whole un-pin slide — the line travels a full viewport
137	  up, crosses fixed chrome, overlaps the next section. Invisible until
138	  measured; shows up as a contrast failure nobody meant.
139	- **Ground or greet.** A pinned stage is fully visible ~1vh *before* its own
140	  progress leaves 0. A plain two-value first cue shows an empty stage for
141	  that whole travel — give the act a ground (image/colour already doing
142	  work) or open with a greet cue.
143	- **Clip time ≠ cue time.** A `scrub` clip is mapped across the stage's
144	  *entire visible life* (default), not across the pinned travel, because the
145	  stage is on screen for a viewport before the pin starts and after it ends.
146	  Cues keep using `p` (they belong to the pin); the clip uses a separately
147	  computed `vp`. Reaching for `data-sc-clip-map="travel"` reintroduces the
148	  freeze — there's almost no reason to.
149	
150	Two more that a harness will not catch by itself:
151	
152	- **Pan overflow must be measured, not assumed.** The rail travels exactly
153	  `scrollWidth - viewport`; a rail narrower than the viewport travels **zero**
154	  and the act reads as a still. `rail.scrollWidth - innerWidth` — check it,
155	  don't guess.
156	- **Parallax rate is hundreds of pixels total, not a viewport fraction** — see
157	  the table above. A rate of 0.35 across three viewport-heights of scroll is
158	  35px: invisible.
159	
160	Composing an act: devices stack (a pinned stage can hold a scrub clip, a
161	parallax layer, a kinetic headline, a spotlight at once), but one thing is the
162	reason the act exists — say that thing in one sentence or the act has none.
163	
164	## The playhead is lerped (§1)
165	
166	The mechanism the whole kit's smoothness rests on, and the one F-012 kept
167	being blamed on. **Scroll never writes `currentTime`.** It writes a *target*,
168	and a standalone rAF loop walks the clip toward that target at a fixed
169	fraction per frame:
170	
171	> *"Wheel events do not arrive at a constant rate, so a 1:1 write reproduces
172	> every gap in them and the clip reads as a stutter rather than a glide."*
173	
174	Three mechanisms, all on by default:
175	
176	- **Lerp 0.18 per frame.** `data-sc-lerp` overrides it, on the mount root for
177	  the whole page or on a single `<video>`. **Clamped to 0.02–1 and never read
178	  as 0** — a 0 lerp is a playhead that never moves. Reach for an override only
179	  when a page's clips are short enough that 0.18 visibly lags the hand.
180	  Worldflight wants 0.12 instead; see [`pace.md`](pace.md).
181	- **Deadband: 8 ms desktop, 20 ms mobile.** A write smaller than that costs a
182	  seek and shows nothing; on a phone it costs more than it shows.
183	- **Seek coalescing.** No seek is queued while the decoder is still resolving
184	  the last one. *"A fast flick otherwise piles seeks up and freezes the clip."*
185	
186	An offscreen clip that has already reached its target stops being touched at
187	all. (Upstream states the offscreen skip without a threshold value; the 0.002
188	figure belongs to `shoot.mjs`'s settle test, below, not to this skip.)
189	
190	This applies to **every** scrub clip on the page, act or worldflight. It is
191	also why the shooter waits for the playhead to arrive before each frame:
192	
193	> *"A frame captured mid-lerp is a frame the page never actually holds."*
194	
195	`shoot.mjs` settles on `|current − target| < 0.002 && !seeking`. Any harness
196	the chain runs against a scrubbed page inherits that requirement — a
197	screenshot taken mid-lerp makes the run unrepeatable, not merely imprecise.
198	
199	Upstream also drops the damping to 1.0 (no smoothing at all) under reduced
200	motion. **That branch does not port: F-011.** The lerp is unconditional here,
201	which is the correct behaviour anyway — it is a smoothing mechanism, not an
202	effect, and turning it off is what produces the stepping fault.
203	
204	## Layered scenes: where the premium feel comes from (§6)
205	
206	Ported from `devices.md` § 6, measured off a reference premium site and proven
207	on a live build. A flat page moves as one sheet; a layered page is a stack of
208	cut-out planes sliding past each other, and *"the eye reads that differential
209	motion as depth before it reads anything else."* It is the single biggest
210	difference between a page that feels built and one that feels assembled, and
211	it costs three transparent images and a multiplier each.
212	
213	- **Plan the planes back to front.** Far ridge, mid ridge, the product, then a
214	  **foreground plane in front of the product**. The product sits between mid
215	  and front, so the foreground overtakes it as the reader scrolls. That
216	  overtaking is the move.
217	- **Small rate differences, not big ones.** The reference hero lags the far
218	  plane **31%** behind the page, the mid plane **17%**, the product **20%**,
219	  and foreground and copy travel at exactly **1×**. Adjacent planes differ by
220	  **10–30%**. Larger stops reading as distance and starts reading as things
221	  sliding around. **Copy always rides at 1×.**
222	- **Shape the foreground for the product.** A straight-edged foreground covers
223	  the product's CTA within a few hundred pixels of scroll. Cut it so it dips
224	  where the product is and rises at the edges, and the button stays in view
225	  two to three times as long.
226	- **Every plane is solid below its silhouette.** Cut-out art that fades to
227	  transparent at the bottom lets the plane behind show through as the planes
228	  separate. Fill each column solid from its first opaque pixel down.
229	- **Fade the section floor.** Planes travel past the section's bottom edge and
230	  are clipped there. A gradient to the page ground over the last 200–300 px,
231	  layered above every plane, hides the clip line at any scroll position.
232	
233	Three traps, each of which cost a round of fixes:
234	
235	- A global `img { max-width: 100% }` shrinks an absolutely positioned plane to
236	  the viewport on phones, so the far layer never shows. **Planes carry
237	  `max-width: none` and a fixed pixel width.**
238	- **Never `transition: transform` on a parallaxed element.** A reveal class is
239	  the usual culprit. The transition eases every per-frame scroll write over
240	  its own duration, and on a phone that reads as the product lagging a full
241	  second behind the thumb. Parallaxed elements transition **opacity only**.
242	- Replacing a plane's art under the same filename ships nothing to a phone
243	  holding the old bytes. **New art gets a new name.**
244	
245	`data-sc-parallax` and a raw scroll multiplier are the same tool in different
246	units. What matters is the **ratio between planes**, not the absolute travel.
247	
248	## The premium fade-in, exactly (§8)
249	
250	The `flow` + `in` device is most of the page, so its defaults decide how the
251	page feels between the acts:
252	
253	| Ingredient | Value |
254	|---|---|
255	| Opacity | 0 → 1 |
256	| Rise | **~14 px** |
257	| Duration | **~620 ms**, ease-out |
258	| Stagger | **30–80 ms**, children in reading order |
259	| Trigger | IntersectionObserver, `-12%` bottom root margin, **fires once** |
260	
261	- **A fade with no rise reads as a loading glitch.** A rise **past 24 px reads
262	  as a slide.** 14 px is the band, not a starting point to tune upward.
263	- The `-12%` margin fires the reveal when the reader is looking, not when the
264	  first pixel clears the fold.
265	- `data-sc-in` is what the engine watches. Without it nothing fires and the
266	  stagger children stay hidden.
267	- **Content that re-hides on the way back up is a defect, not an effect.**
268	- *"Larger, slower, or bouncier is never more premium; the restraint is the
269	  signal."*
270	
271	**A flow section directly after a pinned act takes reduced padding.** The
272	pinned stage needs a full viewport to scroll off, and full `--sc-section`
273	padding on top of that delays the flow section's first content by another
274	screen. The harness will not call it dead scroll — correctly, the stage is
275	moving — and the reader still sees a near-empty screen. Cut the block padding
276	there and start the first reveal near `p = 0`.
277	
278	## Rail settle on `pan` (§3)
279	
280	Lateral travel alone reads as a slideshow on rails. **Give the rail's items a
281	staggered settle driven from `--sc-p`** and they read as a drawer being
282	pulled instead.
283	
284	- **Exempt the first item** — a `pan` act needs its opening content already
285	  present.
286	- **Floor the opacity around 0.55**, so a not-yet-settled card reads as
287	  arriving rather than as failing to load.
288	
289	Upstream gates the settle to `prefers-reduced-motion` — **utgår, F-011**.
290	The settle always runs. What *does* survive from
291	the same passage is the reachability requirement, which is not a motion
292	preference at all: a `pan` rail's transform **is** the navigation, so nothing
293	may zero it and park the act on its first screenful. Every item in a rail
294	stays reachable, and that is checked on the sheet, not assumed.
295	
296	Two more, from the same section:
297	
298	- **Card copy is read while cropped.** Items enter and leave through the
299	  viewport edges, so a heading is half-shown for most of its life, and two
300	  half-headings side by side can read as a third word (`TRACE` beside
301	  `EVALUATE` becoming `RE EVALUATE`). Keep card headings to one or two short
302	  words and expect every line to be read partially cut off.
303	- If three items do not reach half a viewport of overflow, **the fix is more
304	  rail, not wider cards**: put the act's heading in as the first item and a
305	  closing note as the last. Both earn their place, and they add the width the
306	  travel needs.
307	
308	## Devices that cannot share an element (§9)
309	
310	**`magnet`, `parallax` and `cue` all write `transform`.** The magnet writes
311	every frame in its own rAF loop, so it silently wins and the cue's entrance
312	rise is discarded — a visible animation lost to a race, with nothing in the
313	console.
314	
315	- On a magnetic CTA, set **`data-sc-rise="0"`** so the cue writes a no-op
316	  instead of losing to the magnet.
317	- A cued element that wants its own continuous transform drives an **inner
318	  wrapper** from `--sc-p` in CSS, rather than stacking a second device on the
319	  same node.
320	
321	All three pointer devices **interpolate toward** the pointer rather than
322	tracking it directly: *"direct tracking reads as artificial because it carries
323	no momentum."* They stay gated to `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` so
324	touch never fires a false hover — that gate is a pointer-capability query, not
325	a motion preference, and it stands.
326	The reduced-motion half of the same sentence does not port (F-011).
327	
328	## Kinetic type: the mask and the re-split (§5)
329	
330	Each unit slides up from **behind a mask**, so it enters from a clean edge
331	rather than simply fading.
332	
333	- **Line masks must reserve room for descenders.** A mask clipped to the line
334	  box shears the tails off g, y, p and j, *"and that is the single most common
335	  way this effect looks broken."*
336	- **Line splitting measures real line boxes, so it re-runs after
337	  `document.fonts.ready`.** Do not call it on text still loading its face. The
338	  same `fonts.ready` handle earns its place twice over: a webfont swapping in
339	  changes the measured height of every copy block, so anything sized against
340	  those blocks (a scrim plate, a rail) is wrong until it re-measures.
341	- Lines are almost always right; words for a short punch line; characters
342	  approximately never, *"because it turns reading into waiting."*
343	- **One kinetic headline per act, at most.**
344	
345	## What makes a `count` land (§7)
346	
347	- **Ease out, hard.** A cubic ease-out, so most of the distance goes by in the
348	  first third and the last digits settle slowly. *"A linear count reads as a
349	  slot machine."*
350	- **1.2–1.8 s.** Under a second and the reader misses that it moved; past two
351	  and they are waiting for a number they have already guessed.
352	- **Fires at half visibility, once**, so the reader is looking at it when it
353	  starts, and it never re-runs on the way back up.
354	- **Pair it with the fade.** A counter inside a `data-sc-in` stack rises in
355	  with its label and starts ticking as it arrives — *"the same numbers static
356	  on the page read as a spreadsheet."*
357	- Write the target exactly as it should render, commas included; the engine
358	  strips them before parsing and applies `tabular-nums` so the layout does not
359	  jitter.
360	
361	**A concept, fictional or pre-launch brand has no verified figures, so it has
362	no counters.** The device suits a SaaS or agency page and will look good in
363	the score table, *"which is exactly the trap: every number you could put in it
364	would be invented."* Decide this before designing an act around a number, not
365	after. Real brand, real stats, or a different device.
366	
367	## Appendix: pattern vocabulary
368	
369	Named patterns from taste-skill § 10, carried here so orchestrator, builder
370	and reviewer name the same thing. It is a **vocabulary, not a menu** — several
371	entries below are banned as directions elsewhere in the chain (glassmorphism,
372	holographic foil, carousels, gooey menus) and appear here only so a critique
373	can say which trope it is refusing.
374	
375	- **Hero** — Asymmetric Split · Editorial Manifesto · Video/Media Mask ·
376	  Kinetic-Type · Curtain-Reveal · Scroll-Pinned.
377	- **Nav** — Dock Magnification · Magnetic Button (`data-sc-magnet`) · Gooey
378	  Menu · Dynamic Island · Contextual Radial · Floating Speed Dial · Mega Menu
379	  Reveal.
380	- **Layout** — Bento Grid · Masonry · Chroma Grid · Split-Screen Scroll ·
381	  Sticky-Stack Sections.
382	- **Cards** — Parallax Tilt Card (`data-sc-tilt`) · Spotlight Border Card
383	  (`data-sc-spotlight`) · Glassmorphism Panel · Holographic Foil ·
384	  Tinder Swipe Stack · Morphing Modal.
385	- **Scroll** — Sticky Scroll Stack · Horizontal Scroll Hijack (= `pan`) ·
386	  Locomotive / Sequence Scroll (= `scrub`) · Zoom Parallax · Scroll Progress
387	  Path · Liquid Swipe Transition.
388	- **Galleries** — Dome Gallery · Coverflow Carousel · Drag-to-Pan Grid ·
389	  Accordion Image Slider · Hover Image Trail · Glitch Effect Image.
390	- **Type** — Kinetic Marquee · **Text Mask Reveal** (massive type as a
391	  transparent window onto video — this is K2's letter-window) · Text Scramble
392	  · Circular Text Path · Gradient Stroke Animation · Kinetic Typography Grid.
393	- **Micro** — Particle Explosion Button · Liquid Pull-to-Refresh · Skeleton
394	  Shimmer · Directional Hover-Aware Button · Ripple Click · Animated SVG Line
395	  Drawing · Mesh Gradient Background · Lens Blur Depth.
396	
397	Names alone are not permission. A pattern still has to clear the fingerprint
398	gate, the register, and `../motion.md` before it ships.
399	
400	## Never restyle the engine's classes (AB06, 2026-09-03)
401	
402	Theme the engine only through its six colour tokens and two fonts. A project rule on
403	`.sc-stage`, `.sc-copy`, `.sc-scrim` or any other `.sc-*` class silently wins over the
404	engine: the console then says `[scrollcraft] act "…" will not pin: its stage computes
405	position:relative` and every pinned act scrolls away, leaving its spacer as dead scroll.
406	Read the console for `[scrollcraft]` warnings before anything else in Step 5, and run
407	`scripts/scroll_verify.py` — a blind one-shot cannot see either. The engine is opt-in per
408	grammar (scrub, pin, pan); a page that keeps the chain's own single set-piece + shared
409	reveal does not need it.
410
