# The device kit, condensed

Nine ways scroll can drive the page. Pick per beat, never per page: ≥4 device
families, never the same one twice running. Every act publishes `--sc-p` (0–1)
on itself, so bespoke CSS can ride the same value the kit devices use. Full
depth, worked examples, and every trap: `upstream/scroll-craft/.../references/devices.md`.

| # | Device | Syntax | Span / rate | One-line rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `scrub` | `data-sc-act="scrub" data-sc-span="2.6" data-sc-dwell="0.35"` on the section; `data-sc-scrub data-sc-src="…"` on the `<video>` | span 2.2–3.0 for a hero | ≤2 per page. The wheel scrubs a pre-rendered clip; spend it on the open |
| 2 | `pin` | `data-sc-act="pin" data-sc-span="3"` | span ≥1.2 (below that, progress jumps 0→1 in one notch) | The frame holds, copy states cross over inside it |
| 3 | `pan` | `data-sc-act="pan" data-sc-span="3.2"`; rail gets `data-sc-pan="0.08"` | ~1vh per item + 1 | Lateral = breadth, not hierarchy. Overflow must be measured, not assumed |
| 4 | `reveal` | `data-sc-reveal="up|down|left|right|iris" data-sc-reveal-at="0.15 0.55"` | — | `clip-path` wipe = change of state. `iris` once per page at most |
| 5 | `kinetic` | `data-sc-kinetic="lines|words|chars"` on a cued heading | — | Lines almost always right, chars ~never. One kinetic headline per act |
| 6 | `parallax` | `data-sc-parallax="-0.6"` | rate is **hundreds of px total travel**, not a fraction — usable range 0.3–1.5 (framed), 1–2 (full-bleed) | Never on body copy. 3 layers is plenty |
| 7 | `count` | `data-sc-count="0 4,200" data-sc-count-at="0.1 0.5"` | 1.2–1.8s outside an act (`data-sc-count-ms`) | Only real numbers. No verified figure, no counter |
| 8 | `flow` + `in` | `data-sc-in data-sc-stagger="70"` on the wrap | stagger 30–80ms | The rest of the page. Fires once, opacity+14px rise, ~620ms ease-out |
| 9 | pointer: `tilt` / `magnet` / `spotlight` | `data-sc-tilt="7"` (5–9°), `data-sc-magnet="0.28"` (0.2–0.35, CTA only), `data-sc-spotlight` (publishes `--sc-mx`/`--sc-my`) | — | Gated to `(hover:hover) and (pointer:fine)`. Never gated on reduced motion (F-011, superseded 2026-09-07) |

`drift` (`data-sc-drift="#0A0806"` on an act) is not a device, it's a
property: the page ground interpolates toward it while the act is live. 3–5
stops, one theme family. On a page of many *short* acts several can be
part-way through at once — paint grounds per section instead of drifting; see
upstream §10.

## The engine: GSAP + Lenis (house default from 2026-09-24)

**Every new build animates with GSAP** (+ScrollTrigger, SplitText when text is
split) **and Lenis.** Scrollcraft (`scripts/scroll/`) stays only for pages already
built on it — do not port an existing scrollcraft page to GSAP+Lenis just because
it's the new default. **Never mix the two engines on one page**: two scroll owners
is two RAF loops fighting for the same frame. Anton's instruction: GSAP+Lenis for
all animations, applied wherever the motion fits the design and elements of each
page.

Vendored locally from `scripts/motion/vendor/` (gsap 3.15.0, ScrollTrigger,
SplitText, lenis 1.3.26 + `lenis.css`) — copy the whole folder into the build's
`assets/vendor/`; never a CDN at runtime. GSAP 3.13+ including SplitText is free.

The init, verbatim — house deviations from Lenis's own defaults, each explained
once here so no builder reads the Lenis README and takes the default instead:

```js
var lenis = new Lenis({ autoRaf: false, anchors: true, respectReducedMotion: false, lerp: 0.1 });
window.__lenis = lenis;
gsap.ticker.add(function (time) { lenis.raf(time * 1000); });
gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0);
lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update);
```

- **`respectReducedMotion: false`.** Lenis's own default is `true`, which would
  silently switch off all motion for Anton, whose Windows runs with animation
  effects off (house rule F-011 / CARL design decision 2026-09-07). Rörelse spelar
  alltid — motion always plays.
- **`anchors: true`.** Lenis's default is `false`, which breaks in-page anchor
  links silently — no error, they just stop scrolling to the target.
- **`autoRaf: false`, driven by `gsap.ticker`.** `gsap.ticker` is the only RAF
  driver on the page; Lenis's own rAF loop would be a second one racing it.
- **`gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)`** and **`lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)`**
  keep GSAP's tab-blur catch-up off and ScrollTrigger's cached positions synced to
  Lenis's virtual scroll on every frame.
- **`window.__lenis`** is the dev hook every jump-test drives:
  `lenis.scrollTo(el, {immediate:true})`, never `window.scrollTo`.

No `scrollerProxy` (Lenis scrolls the real page, not a virtual container). No CSS
`scroll-behavior: smooth` anywhere — it fights Lenis's own smoothing.

**Iframes.** `lenis.css` sets `pointer-events: none` on iframes while smooth-scroll
is active — wanted behaviour for scroll-driven embeds (a showcase iframe the reader
scrolls *past*). For an embed the reader should scroll *inside*, set
`data-lenis-prevent` on it.

### Scrollcraft device → GSAP equivalent

| Scrollcraft | GSAP + Lenis |
|---|---|
| `scrub` (`data-sc-act=scrub`) | ScrollTrigger `scrub: true` timeline |
| `pin` | `pin: true`, created **once** at init |
| `pan` | pinned timeline, `xPercent` |
| `reveal` | `ScrollTrigger.batch` or a per-element trigger, fail toward visible |
| `kinetic` | SplitText `type:'lines,words,chars', mask:'lines'` + per-word `white-space: nowrap`; the mask needs `padding-bottom` with an equal negative margin so descenders survive |
| `parallax` | `yPercent` scrub |
| `count` | tween on a plain object + `snap` / `gsap.utils.snap` |
| `tilt` / `magnet` | `gsap.quickTo`, gated `(hover: hover)` |
| grid dissolve | `stagger: {grid, from:'random'}` |
| `responsive` (`gsap.matchMedia`) | `gsap.matchMedia()` |

### Load-bearing rules

- Create every ScrollTrigger **in page order.**
- **Never mix `scrub` and `toggleActions` on one trigger.**
- The **last element on the page** uses `end: 'bottom bottom'`.
- **With Lenis, use `scrub: true`, not a numeric scrub.** Lenis is the ONE
  smoothing layer on the page — a numeric scrub value stacks a second lag on top
  of it. Measured jank in V3f's showcase, 2026-09-24.
- **A pin is created once at init and is never killed/recreated on user
  interaction.** V3f's click handler did that and produced a hard, visible
  transition where the pin snapped instead of holding.
- **`end` is set in pixels via a function, with `invalidateOnRefresh: true` —
  never a `'+=Nvh'` string.** ScrollTrigger silently ignores the `vh` suffix on
  that shorthand — measured V3f R5.

### Skills to load before the first line of motion code

In order: `lenis` → `gsap-core` → `gsap-scrolltrigger` → `gsap-timeline` →
`gsap-plugins` (if SplitText/Flip) → `gsap-performance` → `gsap-utils` (if
needed). Plus the UI-skills registry's `ibelick/fixing-motion-performance` — see
[`skill-orchestration.md`](../skill-orchestration.md).

## The cue contract — what verification actually catches you on

`data-sc-cue="from [to [rampIn [rampOut]]]"`, all in act progress 0–1.

| Form | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `"0.2"` | fades in at 0.2, **holds to the end of the act** |
| `"0.1 0.6"` | in, plateau, out (ramps default 30% of window each) |
| `"0 0.78 0"` | **greet**: full opacity at act start, then fades — the hero form |
| `"0 1 0 0"` | **greet and hold**: full at p=0, no ramp either end |

**The plateau is the point.** Without one, a cue is a triangle that touches full
opacity for a single instant, so the reader has to stop on exactly the right
pixel to see the line at full strength and every heading reads slightly faded.
`"0.1 0.9 0.15 0.4"` — fast in, long slow out — is the confident form. Cue
windows on a pinned act **overlap by design**, roughly 15% of the act: the
outgoing line is still fading while the next arrives, and a gap between cues
reads as a loading failure.

Five rules, each one a real bug this fixture has caught:

- **A hero cue needs the greet form.** A plain `"0 0.7"` means the first
  screen every visitor sees has no headline on it.
- **The last act's cue must hold** (one value). A two-value close cue fades
  the CTA out before the page ends.
- **Only the last act may hold.** A one-value cue on a *middle* pinned act
  stays lit through the whole un-pin slide — the line travels a full viewport
  up, crosses fixed chrome, overlaps the next section. Invisible until
  measured; shows up as a contrast failure nobody meant.
- **Ground or greet.** A pinned stage is fully visible ~1vh *before* its own
  progress leaves 0. A plain two-value first cue shows an empty stage for
  that whole travel — give the act a ground (image/colour already doing
  work) or open with a greet cue.
- **Clip time ≠ cue time.** A `scrub` clip is mapped across the stage's
  *entire visible life* (default), not across the pinned travel, because the
  stage is on screen for a viewport before the pin starts and after it ends.
  Cues keep using `p` (they belong to the pin); the clip uses a separately
  computed `vp`. Reaching for `data-sc-clip-map="travel"` reintroduces the
  freeze — there's almost no reason to.

Two more that a harness will not catch by itself:

- **Pan overflow must be measured, not assumed.** The rail travels exactly
  `scrollWidth - viewport`; a rail narrower than the viewport travels **zero**
  and the act reads as a still. `rail.scrollWidth - innerWidth` — check it,
  don't guess.
- **Parallax rate is hundreds of pixels total, not a viewport fraction** — see
  the table above. A rate of 0.35 across three viewport-heights of scroll is
  35px: invisible.

Composing an act: devices stack (a pinned stage can hold a scrub clip, a
parallax layer, a kinetic headline, a spotlight at once), but one thing is the
reason the act exists — say that thing in one sentence or the act has none.

## The playhead is lerped (§1)

The mechanism the whole kit's smoothness rests on, and the one F-012 kept
being blamed on. **Scroll never writes `currentTime`.** It writes a *target*,
and a standalone rAF loop walks the clip toward that target at a fixed
fraction per frame:

> *"Wheel events do not arrive at a constant rate, so a 1:1 write reproduces
> every gap in them and the clip reads as a stutter rather than a glide."*

Three mechanisms, all on by default:

- **Lerp 0.18 per frame.** `data-sc-lerp` overrides it, on the mount root for
  the whole page or on a single `<video>`. **Clamped to 0.02–1 and never read
  as 0** — a 0 lerp is a playhead that never moves. Reach for an override only
  when a page's clips are short enough that 0.18 visibly lags the hand.
  Worldflight wants 0.12 instead; see [`pace.md`](pace.md).
- **Deadband: 8 ms desktop, 20 ms mobile.** A write smaller than that costs a
  seek and shows nothing; on a phone it costs more than it shows.
- **Seek coalescing.** No seek is queued while the decoder is still resolving
  the last one. *"A fast flick otherwise piles seeks up and freezes the clip."*

An offscreen clip that has already reached its target stops being touched at
all. (Upstream states the offscreen skip without a threshold value; the 0.002
figure belongs to `shoot.mjs`'s settle test, below, not to this skip.)

This applies to **every** scrub clip on the page, act or worldflight. It is
also why the shooter waits for the playhead to arrive before each frame:

> *"A frame captured mid-lerp is a frame the page never actually holds."*

`shoot.mjs` settles on `|current − target| < 0.002 && !seeking`. Any harness
the chain runs against a scrubbed page inherits that requirement — a
screenshot taken mid-lerp makes the run unrepeatable, not merely imprecise.

Upstream also drops the damping to 1.0 (no smoothing at all) under reduced
motion. **That branch does not port: F-011.** The lerp is unconditional here,
which is the correct behaviour anyway — it is a smoothing mechanism, not an
effect, and turning it off is what produces the stepping fault.

## Layered scenes: where the premium feel comes from (§6)

Ported from `devices.md` § 6, measured off a reference premium site and proven
on a live build. A flat page moves as one sheet; a layered page is a stack of
cut-out planes sliding past each other, and *"the eye reads that differential
motion as depth before it reads anything else."* It is the single biggest
difference between a page that feels built and one that feels assembled, and
it costs three transparent images and a multiplier each.

- **Plan the planes back to front.** Far ridge, mid ridge, the product, then a
  **foreground plane in front of the product**. The product sits between mid
  and front, so the foreground overtakes it as the reader scrolls. That
  overtaking is the move.
- **Small rate differences, not big ones.** The reference hero lags the far
  plane **31%** behind the page, the mid plane **17%**, the product **20%**,
  and foreground and copy travel at exactly **1×**. Adjacent planes differ by
  **10–30%**. Larger stops reading as distance and starts reading as things
  sliding around. **Copy always rides at 1×.**
- **Shape the foreground for the product.** A straight-edged foreground covers
  the product's CTA within a few hundred pixels of scroll. Cut it so it dips
  where the product is and rises at the edges, and the button stays in view
  two to three times as long.
- **Every plane is solid below its silhouette.** Cut-out art that fades to
  transparent at the bottom lets the plane behind show through as the planes
  separate. Fill each column solid from its first opaque pixel down.
- **Fade the section floor.** Planes travel past the section's bottom edge and
  are clipped there. A gradient to the page ground over the last 200–300 px,
  layered above every plane, hides the clip line at any scroll position.

Three traps, each of which cost a round of fixes:

- A global `img { max-width: 100% }` shrinks an absolutely positioned plane to
  the viewport on phones, so the far layer never shows. **Planes carry
  `max-width: none` and a fixed pixel width.**
- **Never `transition: transform` on a parallaxed element.** A reveal class is
  the usual culprit. The transition eases every per-frame scroll write over
  its own duration, and on a phone that reads as the product lagging a full
  second behind the thumb. Parallaxed elements transition **opacity only**.
- Replacing a plane's art under the same filename ships nothing to a phone
  holding the old bytes. **New art gets a new name.**

`data-sc-parallax` and a raw scroll multiplier are the same tool in different
units. What matters is the **ratio between planes**, not the absolute travel.

## The premium fade-in, exactly (§8)

The `flow` + `in` device is most of the page, so its defaults decide how the
page feels between the acts:

| Ingredient | Value |
|---|---|
| Opacity | 0 → 1 |
| Rise | **~14 px** |
| Duration | **~620 ms**, ease-out |
| Stagger | **30–80 ms**, children in reading order |
| Trigger | IntersectionObserver, `-12%` bottom root margin, **fires once** |

- **A fade with no rise reads as a loading glitch.** A rise **past 24 px reads
  as a slide.** 14 px is the band, not a starting point to tune upward.
- The `-12%` margin fires the reveal when the reader is looking, not when the
  first pixel clears the fold.
- `data-sc-in` is what the engine watches. Without it nothing fires and the
  stagger children stay hidden.
- **Content that re-hides on the way back up is a defect, not an effect.**
- *"Larger, slower, or bouncier is never more premium; the restraint is the
  signal."*

**A flow section directly after a pinned act takes reduced padding.** The
pinned stage needs a full viewport to scroll off, and full `--sc-section`
padding on top of that delays the flow section's first content by another
screen. The harness will not call it dead scroll — correctly, the stage is
moving — and the reader still sees a near-empty screen. Cut the block padding
there and start the first reveal near `p = 0`.

## Rail settle on `pan` (§3)

Lateral travel alone reads as a slideshow on rails. **Give the rail's items a
staggered settle driven from `--sc-p`** and they read as a drawer being
pulled instead.

- **Exempt the first item** — a `pan` act needs its opening content already
  present.
- **Floor the opacity around 0.55**, so a not-yet-settled card reads as
  arriving rather than as failing to load.

Upstream gates the settle to `prefers-reduced-motion` — **utgår, F-011**.
The settle always runs. What *does* survive from
the same passage is the reachability requirement, which is not a motion
preference at all: a `pan` rail's transform **is** the navigation, so nothing
may zero it and park the act on its first screenful. Every item in a rail
stays reachable, and that is checked on the sheet, not assumed.

Two more, from the same section:

- **Card copy is read while cropped.** Items enter and leave through the
  viewport edges, so a heading is half-shown for most of its life, and two
  half-headings side by side can read as a third word (`TRACE` beside
  `EVALUATE` becoming `RE EVALUATE`). Keep card headings to one or two short
  words and expect every line to be read partially cut off.
- If three items do not reach half a viewport of overflow, **the fix is more
  rail, not wider cards**: put the act's heading in as the first item and a
  closing note as the last. Both earn their place, and they add the width the
  travel needs.

## Devices that cannot share an element (§9)

**`magnet`, `parallax` and `cue` all write `transform`.** The magnet writes
every frame in its own rAF loop, so it silently wins and the cue's entrance
rise is discarded — a visible animation lost to a race, with nothing in the
console.

- On a magnetic CTA, set **`data-sc-rise="0"`** so the cue writes a no-op
  instead of losing to the magnet.
- A cued element that wants its own continuous transform drives an **inner
  wrapper** from `--sc-p` in CSS, rather than stacking a second device on the
  same node.

All three pointer devices **interpolate toward** the pointer rather than
tracking it directly: *"direct tracking reads as artificial because it carries
no momentum."* They stay gated to `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` so
touch never fires a false hover — that gate is a pointer-capability query, not
a motion preference, and it stands.
The reduced-motion half of the same sentence does not port (F-011).

## Kinetic type: the mask and the re-split (§5)

Each unit slides up from **behind a mask**, so it enters from a clean edge
rather than simply fading.

- **Line masks must reserve room for descenders.** A mask clipped to the line
  box shears the tails off g, y, p and j, *"and that is the single most common
  way this effect looks broken."*
- **Line splitting measures real line boxes, so it re-runs after
  `document.fonts.ready`.** Do not call it on text still loading its face. The
  same `fonts.ready` handle earns its place twice over: a webfont swapping in
  changes the measured height of every copy block, so anything sized against
  those blocks (a scrim plate, a rail) is wrong until it re-measures.
- Lines are almost always right; words for a short punch line; characters
  approximately never, *"because it turns reading into waiting."*
- **One kinetic headline per act, at most.**

## What makes a `count` land (§7)

- **Ease out, hard.** A cubic ease-out, so most of the distance goes by in the
  first third and the last digits settle slowly. *"A linear count reads as a
  slot machine."*
- **1.2–1.8 s.** Under a second and the reader misses that it moved; past two
  and they are waiting for a number they have already guessed.
- **Fires at half visibility, once**, so the reader is looking at it when it
  starts, and it never re-runs on the way back up.
- **Pair it with the fade.** A counter inside a `data-sc-in` stack rises in
  with its label and starts ticking as it arrives — *"the same numbers static
  on the page read as a spreadsheet."*
- Write the target exactly as it should render, commas included; the engine
  strips them before parsing and applies `tabular-nums` so the layout does not
  jitter.

**A concept, fictional or pre-launch brand has no verified figures, so it has
no counters.** The device suits a SaaS or agency page and will look good in
the score table, *"which is exactly the trap: every number you could put in it
would be invented."* Decide this before designing an act around a number, not
after. Real brand, real stats, or a different device.

## Appendix: pattern vocabulary

Named patterns from taste-skill § 10, carried here so orchestrator, builder
and reviewer name the same thing. It is a **vocabulary, not a menu** — several
entries below are banned as directions elsewhere in the chain (glassmorphism,
holographic foil, carousels, gooey menus) and appear here only so a critique
can say which trope it is refusing.

- **Hero** — Asymmetric Split · Editorial Manifesto · Video/Media Mask ·
  Kinetic-Type · Curtain-Reveal · Scroll-Pinned.
- **Nav** — Dock Magnification · Magnetic Button (`data-sc-magnet`) · Gooey
  Menu · Dynamic Island · Contextual Radial · Floating Speed Dial · Mega Menu
  Reveal.
- **Layout** — Bento Grid · Masonry · Chroma Grid · Split-Screen Scroll ·
  Sticky-Stack Sections.
- **Cards** — Parallax Tilt Card (`data-sc-tilt`) · Spotlight Border Card
  (`data-sc-spotlight`) · Glassmorphism Panel · Holographic Foil ·
  Tinder Swipe Stack · Morphing Modal.
- **Scroll** — Sticky Scroll Stack · Horizontal Scroll Hijack (= `pan`) ·
  Locomotive / Sequence Scroll (= `scrub`) · Zoom Parallax · Scroll Progress
  Path · Liquid Swipe Transition.
- **Galleries** — Dome Gallery · Coverflow Carousel · Drag-to-Pan Grid ·
  Accordion Image Slider · Hover Image Trail · Glitch Effect Image.
- **Type** — Kinetic Marquee · **Text Mask Reveal** (massive type as a
  transparent window onto video — this is K2's letter-window) · Text Scramble
  · Circular Text Path · Gradient Stroke Animation · Kinetic Typography Grid.
- **Micro** — Particle Explosion Button · Liquid Pull-to-Refresh · Skeleton
  Shimmer · Directional Hover-Aware Button · Ripple Click · Animated SVG Line
  Drawing · Mesh Gradient Background · Lens Blur Depth.

Names alone are not permission. A pattern still has to clear the fingerprint
gate, the register, and `../motion.md` before it ships.

## Never restyle the engine's classes (AB06, 2026-09-03)

Theme the engine only through its six colour tokens and two fonts. A project rule on
`.sc-stage`, `.sc-copy`, `.sc-scrim` or any other `.sc-*` class silently wins over the
engine: the console then says `[scrollcraft] act "…" will not pin: its stage computes
position:relative` and every pinned act scrolls away, leaving its spacer as dead scroll.
Read the console for `[scrollcraft]` warnings before anything else in Step 5, and run
`scripts/scroll_verify.py` — a blind one-shot cannot see either. The engine is opt-in per
grammar (scrub, pin, pan); a page that keeps the chain's own single set-piece + shared
reveal does not need it.

122	|---|---|---|
123	| Short acts, hard cuts | Adrenaline, pulse, impatience | Acts under 1.4 vh, no `pin`, `dwell` at 0 |

158	Registry: `VAULT/wiki/projects/_index/design-fingerprints.md`, per-vault,

163	|---|---|---|

165	| 2 | Nav treatment | What the chrome is and what it's for |
166	| 3 | Hero device | What the first screen does |
167	| 4 | Act-sequence shape | Device order, act count, total viewport-heights |
168	| 5 | Close pattern | How the last screen behaves, what the CTA sits in |
169	| 6 | Signature move | The one bespoke interaction, in a phrase |
170

174	more out of the remaining 5 against each row. If the plan fails, **change
175	the plan, not the log** — rewriting a row to fit is what makes it worthless.
176	
177	**Row format** — one row per shipped build, all six dimensions plus a world
178	note and the path: `| Build | Grammar | Nav | Hero device | Act-sequence
179	shape | Close pattern | Signature move | Register | World / palette | Path |`
180

182	
183	> *"A build that has been superseded stays in the table, because the space it
184	> occupies is still occupied."*
185	
186	A replaced, retired or rejected build keeps its row. The registry does not
187	record what is live; it records what surface has already been taken, and a
188	surface stays taken whether or not the build that claimed it is still up.
189	Deleting a row silently frees a shape for reuse, which is the same failure as
190	editing one to make room — *"never edit a row to make room for it. If a
191	planned build fails, change the plan."*
192	
193	**Fill every column.** A row with blanks cannot be scored 4-of-6 against, so
194	it weakens the gate for every build after it.
195	
196	**Keep a "what is taken" list beside the table.** Add a bullet whenever a
197	build claims something a later build should avoid reusing: a grammar, a nav
198	treatment, a close pattern, a signature move, an act-count-and-length band.
199	*"The shared columns are what the next build inherits as a constraint, so
200	writing them down is the whole point."*
201	
202	After shipping, append the row and say what it shares with prior rows — the
203	shared columns are exactly what the *next* build has to avoid.

cheapest emotional instrument in the kit and the one most often left at
default."*

| Pacing | Reads as | Built with |
|---|---|---|
| Short acts, hard cuts | Adrenaline, pulse, impatience | Acts under 1.4 vh, no `pin`, `dwell` at 0 |
| A long pin | Held breath, pressure, attention | `data-sc-span` 3+, overlapping cues, one idea |
| An empty viewport before a reveal | Silence before the drop | A ground-only act, no cue until the next one |
| A slow settle mid-act | The shot landing | `data-sc-dwell` 0.35–0.6, cue peak on the settle |
| A fast cue with a long plateau | Confidence, arrival | `data-sc-cue="0.1 0.9 0.08 0.4"` |
| A slow ramp in | Hesitation, dawning | Long `rampIn` — **once per page**, it is close to feeling broken |

Four rules follow:

- **Silence must be authored, not left over.** *"An empty screen you meant
  reads as anticipation. An empty screen you did not mean reads as a page that
  failed to load, and the harness reports both as dead scroll."* If the empty
  viewport before the peak is deliberate, **say so in `BRIEF.md`** so the
  verification pass can tell it from dead scroll. This is the sentence that
  keeps `scroll_verify.py`'s `blankBands` check from being either useless or a
  false alarm.
- **Give the peak room.** The peak act has the largest span on the page by a
  visible margin. *"If every act is 2.2 vh, the page has no shape, whatever
  the curve in BRIEF.md says."*
- **Compress the administrative parts.** Specs, logistics, FAQ, credentials
  are information, not experience — flow sections at short stagger, never
  pinned acts with dwell. Spending scroll on them spends the visitor's
  patience on the part they will not remember.
- **A continuous world is the exception to pacing variety.** All of the above
  is about a page of *acts*. A worldflight is one camera move, and *"a camera
  that changes speed between legs reads as broken rather than as
  expressive."* There, hold one pace and let the peak carry the shape by being
  the single long leg — [`pace.md`](pace.md).

The total-length budget stays **8–14 viewport-heights**. Pacing is how that
budget is spent, not permission to spend more: *"a page that needs 20 vh to
land its curve has too many acts, not too little room."*

## The fingerprint gate

Registry: `VAULT/wiki/projects/_index/design-fingerprints.md`, per-vault,
starting from whatever rows already exist — not repeating **yourself** across
builds, not a universal constraint. **Six dimensions**, recorded per row:

| # | Dimension | What it records |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Grammar | Which of `grammars.md`, or a named new one |
| 2 | Nav treatment | What the chrome is and what it's for |
| 3 | Hero device | What the first screen does |
| 4 | Act-sequence shape | Device order, act count, total viewport-heights |
| 5 | Close pattern | How the last screen behaves, what the CTA sits in |
| 6 | Signature move | The one bespoke interaction, in a phrase |

**The gate: a new build must differ from EVERY existing row on at least 4 of
the 6** — four against each row individually, not averaged across the table.
Dimension 6 is free (unique by definition), so the gate really asks for 3
more out of the remaining 5 against each row. If the plan fails, **change
the plan, not the log** — rewriting a row to fit is what makes it worthless.

**Row format** — one row per shipped build, all six dimensions plus a world
note and the path: `| Build | Grammar | Nav | Hero device | Act-sequence
shape | Close pattern | Signature move | Register | World / palette | Path |`

**Rows are append-only.** From upstream `templates/FINGERPRINTS.md`:

> *"A build that has been superseded stays in the table, because the space it
> occupies is still occupied."*

A replaced, retired or rejected build keeps its row. The registry does not
record what is live; it records what surface has already been taken, and a
surface stays taken whether or not the build that claimed it is still up.
Deleting a row silently frees a shape for reuse, which is the same failure as
editing one to make room — *"never edit a row to make room for it. If a
planned build fails, change the plan."*

**Fill every column.** A row with blanks cannot be scored 4-of-6 against, so
it weakens the gate for every build after it.

**Keep a "what is taken" list beside the table.** Add a bullet whenever a
build claims something a later build should avoid reusing: a grammar, a nav
treatment, a close pattern, a signature move, an act-count-and-length band.
*"The shared columns are what the next build inherits as a constraint, so
writing them down is the whole point."*

After shipping, append the row and say what it shares with prior rows — the
shared columns are exactly what the *next* build has to avoid.

109	
110	Grammar has been spent hard. Chaptered editorial now has five rows here (r1 K4, r2 R2, R3,
111	R4, r4 M2) on top of the four seed rows, filmic one-shot has four (r6 A-K1, B-K1,
112	B-K1-nogate, r7 B-K1) on top of two seed rows, and typographic poster has five (r1 K3, r2
113	R6, r6 A-K2 and B-K2, r7 B-K2). Continuous world is a five-row family (M1, V1, V2, V3,
114	V3b) that also shares nav treatment and close pattern by construction, because every r5
115	variant inherited M1's chrome and its two closing objects; those five rows clear the gate
116	against each other only on hero device, act shape and signature move, which is exactly 3
117	of the 5 non-free dimensions, the bare minimum. A sixth build in that family would have
118	nowhere left to differ.
119	
120	Two nav patterns repeat across rounds and should be treated as used up: the thin
121	scrolling top row with wordmark and contact (M1, V1, V2, V3, V3b) and the fixed minimal
122	bar with logo left and contact right that darkens or lightens per ground (r6 A-K1, B-K1,
123	B-K1-nogate, r7 B-K1). Two hero devices likewise: the full-bleed blue-hour photograph
124	with a light-serif headline in the water (four rows) and the crushed poster wordmark with
125	the example screenshots showing through or beside the letters (four rows). The r7 rows
126	record their own shared dimensions honestly — each clears the gate at exactly 4 of 6
127	against its r6 predecessor, with grammar and nav knowingly shared — so a v3 of either
128	concept cannot reuse the hero device, the act shape or the close as well.
129	
130	Ten rows carried `?` in Register when the r1–r7 block was first appended: r2 R3, R4 and
131	R5, the r3 build, r4 M1 and M2, and r5 V1, V2, V3 and V3b. Those cells' own files name
132	grammar, world and palette but never a register from the six-name vocabulary, and no
133	sibling file names it for them either. On 2026-09-09 the column was filled for all ten by
134	reading each cell's `index.html` directly (and, for the r3 build and r4 M2, its 1440 fold
135	as pixels) against `design/SKILL.md`'s register table and its "what varies with register"
136	markers: face, grain, buttons versus typeset links, ground and subject. Every one of the
137	ten reads as **modern clean** — one lineage, sans display with mono as register only, no
138	serif and no grain anywhere, one blue accent, ledgers over cards, and a precision subject
139	— which is the same read the registry already recorded for r1 K1, K2, K5, K6 and r2 R1
140	and R2. Each cell states the file it was derived from, so the derivation is auditable and
141	declared as post-hoc, exactly like the seven seed rows above.

# Design fingerprint registry

The fingerprint gate for scroll-choreographed Persuade/Experience builds. See
`.agents/skills/design/references/scroll/feel-and-fingerprint.md` § The
fingerprint gate for the rule: **a new build must differ from EVERY existing
row on at least 4 of the 6 dimension columns**, checked row by row, not
averaged across the table. If a planned build fails the gate, change the
plan, not this file — rewriting a row to make a new build fit is the one
thing that makes this registry worthless.

Seeded 2026-09-03 with one row per existing example site in
`anti-slop-design/sites/`. These sites predate scroll-craft integration and
were not built against the nine-device kit or the eight named grammars — the
Grammar, Signature move and Register columns below are an honest read of what
each page actually does, mapped onto scroll-craft's vocabulary after the
fact, not a claim that they were built to it. Where a site has no bespoke
interaction beyond an ordinary reveal-on-scroll, the Signature move column
says `none` — that is a finding, not a gap in the audit.

| Build | Grammar | Nav treatment | Hero device | Act-sequence shape | Close pattern | Signature move | Register | World / palette | Path |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Calyx | Chaptered editorial | Static (non-sticky) border-b header, 3-col grid: edition kicker · centred wordmark · two text anchors | Full-bleed botanical photo, gradient scrim, headline lead-corner bottom-left, kicker+copy trail-corner bottom-right | ~8 sections: hero > manifesto/quote > duo photo pair > index/commission ledger (`.01`–`.04`) > immersion photo break > testimonial ledger > commission CTA | Dark-inverted section, mailto set as huge italic display type with arrow; 4-col colophon footer | none — plain IntersectionObserver fade/rise reveal and ordinary image-hover scale only | Editorial print | Cardo (display) + PT Mono (kicker); cream / bone / moss / ink / rust | `anti-slop-design/sites/calyx.html` |
| Hōrai | Filmic one-shot | Fixed bar, transparent → dark-blurred on scroll; wordmark + "RESERVATIONS" button | Full-bleed JS-parallax photo, giant wordmark, JP kicker, two-column lede | ~7 sections: hero > the house (word-lit lede) > pinned scroll-scrubbed quote chapter > set menus (3 numbered courses) > photo spread > the room (parallax) > reservations CTA | Dark section, "book.horai.se" as huge typeset link + mailto, address, 3-col colophon | Pinned quote set-piece: kicker + gold rules + JP glyphs + blockquote scrub in/out on a bell-curve proximity-to-viewport-center function, independent per-element stagger (blur, scale, translate, tracking), `?preview=quote` hook | Cinematic dark | Cinzel + Vollkorn + Noto Serif JP; paper / walnut / lacquer / jade | `anti-slop-design/sites/horai.html` |

## Reading this table before a new build

Three grammar collisions already exist among these seven rows: Calyx,
Hyperborea and Vintergatan all read as chaptered editorial, and Vinterspelen
leans the same way with a gallery inflection. A new chaptered-editorial build
has to clear 3 more dimensions against **each** of those four rows
individually — nav treatment and hero device are the two that repeat across
them most (folio/edition-strip nav, type-in-photo or split-poster heroes), so
those are the columns most likely to collide again. Hōrai and Tidvatten share
grammar (filmic one-shot), a fixed minimal bar, a JS-parallax full-bleed
hero, and a bell-curve-scrub pinned set-piece as their signature move's
underlying mechanism — a third filmic one-shot build with a scrub-driven
pinned set-piece would need a genuinely different mechanism for the move, not
just different numbers on screen, to clear dimension 6 meaningfully even
though the gate counts it as free.

`before-ai-slop.html` is not a build to avoid colliding with — it is the
negative reference. Any real build should differ from it on every dimension
by construction.

## Alunix concept builds, rounds 1–7 (appended 2026-09-09)

Twenty-nine rows, one per built `index.html` under `anti-slop-design/tests/alunix-*`.
Every column is derived from the cell's own files: the built HTML (nav markup, section
list, `data-sc-act` attributes, `:root` custom properties, font links), its `NOTES.md`
or `BRIEF.md`, and its desktop fold screenshot read as an image. Where a cell's own
files carry no evidence for a column, the cell says `?` rather than a guess — that is a
finding about the cell's documentation, not a licence to treat the dimension as free.

Duplicates were excluded, not counted twice: `alunix-ab-r6/board/cells/*` are byte-identical
copies of the seven r6 runs, `alunix-ab-r7/board/cells/K1-1` and `K2-1` are byte-identical

Rounds 1–2 and 6 predate scroll-craft integration in those cells (no `data-sc-*` in the
markup); their act shapes are hand-rolled. Rounds 3–5 and 7 run the engine. In r6 and r7,
arm A is the Claude-native control (Anthropic's `frontend-design` system prompt, no skills,
no hooks) and arm B is this chain; `B-K1-nogate` is the r6 chain run where the gate never
fired, kept as its own row because it is a separate build.

variant inherited M1's chrome and its two closing objects; those five rows clear the gate
against each other only on hero device, act shape and signature move, which is exactly 3
of the 5 non-free dimensions, the bare minimum. A sixth build in that family would have
nowhere left to differ.

scrolling top row with wordmark and contact (M1, V1, V2, V3, V3b) and the fixed minimal
bar with logo left and contact right that darkens or lightens per ground (r6 A-K1, B-K1,

the example screenshots showing through or beside the letters (four rows). The r7 rows
record their own shared dimensions honestly — each clears the gate at exactly 4 of 6
against its r6 predecessor, with grammar and nav knowingly shared — so a v3 of either
concept cannot reuse the hero device, the act shape or the close as well.

R5, the r3 build, r4 M1 and M2, and r5 V1, V2, V3 and V3b. Those cells' own files name

sibling file names it for them either. On 2026-09-09 the column was filled for all ten by
reading each cell's `index.html` directly (and, for the r3 build and r4 M2, its 1440 fold
as pixels) against `design/SKILL.md`'s register table and its "what varies with register"
markers: face, grain, buttons versus typeset links, ground and subject. Every one of the
ten reads as **modern clean** — one lineage, sans display with mono as register only, no
serif and no grain anywhere, one blue accent, ledgers over cards, and a precision subject
— which is the same read the registry already recorded for r1 K1, K2, K5, K6 and r2 R1
and R2. Each cell states the file it was derived from, so the derivation is auditable and
declared as post-hoc, exactly like the seven seed rows above.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="sv">
<head>

:root{

  --body:16px;
  --body-30:clamp(1.5rem, 1.347rem + 0.653vw, 2rem);
  --caption:13px;
  --cellpad:20px;
}

*{box-sizing:border-box;}
html{color-scheme:light;}
body{
  margin:0;
  background:#000;
  color:var(--ink);
  font-family:"Geist","Arial",system-ui,sans-serif;
  font-weight:500;
  line-height:1.3;
  -webkit-font-smoothing:antialiased;
  overflow-x:hidden;
}
img{display:block;max-width:100%;}
.mono{font-family:"Geist Mono","Consolas",monospace;font-weight:400;}
h1,h2,h3,p,ol,ul,figure{margin:0;padding:0;}
a{color:inherit;}
.sr-only{position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;padding:0;margin:-1px;overflow:hidden;clip:rect(0,0,0,0);white-space:nowrap;border:0;}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------- rutverket shell */
.rutverk{max-width:1440px;margin:0 auto;background:#000;}
.rutverk > section{scroll-margin-top:48px;}

.g{display:grid;gap:1px;background:#000;}
.cell{background:var(--paper);padding:var(--cellpad);position:relative;overflow:hidden;}
.cell--pad0{padding:0;}
.cell--ink{background:var(--ink);color:var(--paper);}
.cell--black{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);}
.cell--grey{background:var(--grey);color:var(--ink);}
.cell--mint{background:var(--mint);color:var(--black);}
.cell--rust{background:var(--rust);color:var(--paper);}
.cell--lacquer{background:var(--lacquer);color:var(--paper);}

.g12{grid-template-columns:repeat(12,1fr);}
@media (max-width:1199px){
  .g12{grid-template-columns:repeat(6,1fr);}
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  .g12{grid-template-columns:1fr;}
  .g12 > *{grid-column:1 / -1 !important;}
}

.c-2{grid-column:span 2;}
.c-3{grid-column:span 3;}
.c-4{grid-column:span 4;}
.c-5{grid-column:span 5;}
.c-6{grid-column:span 6;}
.c-7{grid-column:span 7;}
.c-8{grid-column:span 8;}
.c-12{grid-column:span 12;}
@media (max-width:1199px){

.headline-50{font-size:var(--headline-50);line-height:.8;letter-spacing:-.04em;font-weight:500;}
.headline-40{font-size:var(--headline-40);line-height:1;letter-spacing:-.04em;font-weight:500;}
.headline-20{font-size:var(--headline-20);line-height:1;letter-spacing:-.04em;font-weight:500;}

.body{font-size:var(--body);line-height:1.3;letter-spacing:-.02em;}
.body-30{font-size:var(--body-30);line-height:1.1;letter-spacing:-.02em;}

.tnum{font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- topline */
.topline{
  position:sticky;top:0;z-index:40;height:48px;max-width:1440px;margin:0 auto;

   owned by ScrollTrigger's own pinSpacing (desktop matchMedia branch,
   RORELSE-SPEC.md §2); hero-wrap just needs to size to its content so a
   no-JS/pre-JS view still shows one full stage, not a dead 90svh gap. */
.hero-wrap{position:relative;max-width:1440px;margin:0 auto;}
.hero-stage{
  position:relative;height:calc(100svh - 48px);
  display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;grid-template-rows:1fr 1fr;
  gap:1px;background:#000;
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  /* Mobile drops the pin: no extra scroll-span, no sticky stage. The four
     cells stack in normal flow (each already min-height:60vw, so the
     stack is naturally taller than one screen) and the card flips against
     that natural scroll distance instead of a dedicated dead-space span. */

.hero-oh{background:var(--grey);}
.hero-nv{background:var(--grey);}
.hero-nh{background:var(--mint);}
.hero-h1{max-width:14ch;}

.dither-layer{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;}
.color-layer{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;}

/* card: a physical object (light stock, ink edge, hard offset shadow) so
   it reads against a black cell instead of disappearing into it. ~1.6x
   the R1 size at 1440 (was ~340px wide, now ~520px), 85:55 kept. */
.card-anchor{
  position:absolute;left:75%;top:50%;
  width:min(36vw,520px);
  aspect-ratio:85/55;
  transform:translate(-50%,-50%);

@media (max-width:767px){ .card-anchor{left:50%;top:120vw;width:min(74vw,380px);} }

.face{

  backface-visibility:hidden;
  border:1px solid #000;

   that is a photo edge-to-edge reads as "the photo", not as "a light
   stock object sitting on the cell" - the mat is what makes the white
   stock actually visible against a black ÖH ground. */
.face--front{background:#fff;padding:6%;}
/* R6 bugfix: kontakt's front is a <button> wrapping <span>s (spans, unlike
   hero's <div>s, default to display:inline) - an inline, merely

.card-mark{font-size:clamp(20px,2.6vw,32px);letter-spacing:-.02em;margin:0;}
.card-kicker{font-family:"Geist Mono";font-weight:400;font-size:clamp(11px,1.1vw,14px);opacity:.65;margin:2px 0 0;}

.process-title{margin:0 0 18px;max-width:11ch;}
.process-lock{max-width:32ch;opacity:.8;}
.process-image{position:relative;margin-top:32px;aspect-ratio:1/1;width:100%;max-width:680px;border:1px solid #000;overflow:hidden;}
.process-right{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);padding:0;}
.process-steps{list-style:none;}
.process-row-item{display:grid;grid-template-columns:56px 1fr;gap:14px;padding:22px var(--cellpad);border-top:1px solid #000;}
.process-row-item:first-child{border-top:none;}
.process-num{font-family:"Geist Mono";font-weight:400;font-size:13px;padding-top:4px;}
.process-step-title{margin:0 0 6px;}
.process-p{color:#bdbdbd;max-width:56ch;font-size:15px;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- exempelcase */
/* R5 §A bugfix: 0.6x bottom padding (12px) was less than the SplitText
   mask-breathe allowance (0.16em, ~16-20px at this clamp size) needs to
   clear the word's own descenders before the cell's overflow:hidden edge
   - verify_motion.py's legibility scan caught the word's rendered box
   (with its mask wrapper's padding-bottom) genuinely sitting a few px
   below the cell's clip boundary at every scroll position (0vh visible,
   not >=40vh). Matching the top padding removes the clip entirely. */
.case-word-cell{padding:calc(var(--cellpad)*1.4) var(--cellpad) calc(var(--cellpad)*1.4 + 4px);overflow:hidden;}
.case-word-cell .headline-50{max-width:100%;}

/* R5 §B1: väljaren - två knappar, skarpa 1440x900-vyer, ingen beskärande zoom */
.case-picker-cell{padding:0 var(--cellpad) calc(var(--cellpad)*1.2);background:#000;}
.case-picker{display:grid;gap:1px;background:#000;}
.case-choice{
  display:block;width:100%;margin:0;padding:0;border:0;background:var(--paper);color:inherit;
  font:inherit;text-align:left;cursor:pointer;-webkit-appearance:none;appearance:none;
}
.case-choice-frame{position:relative;display:block;aspect-ratio:16/10;overflow:hidden;background:var(--grey);}
.case-choice-frame img{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;transform:scale(1);transition:transform .7s cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1);will-change:transform;}
@media (hover:hover){
  .case-choice:hover .case-choice-frame img,
  .case-choice:focus-visible .case-choice-frame img{transform:scale(1.04);}
}
.case-choice:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--mint);outline-offset:-2px;}
.case-choice-meta{display:block;padding:16px var(--cellpad) 20px;border-bottom:4px solid transparent;}
.case-choice[aria-pressed="true"] .case-choice-meta{border-bottom-color:var(--mint);}
.case-choice-meta .h3{display:block;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:22px;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- showcase (B2) */
.showcase-stage{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr;gap:1px;background:#000;}
@media (min-width:768px){ .showcase-stage{grid-template-columns:7fr 5fr;} }
.showcase-embed-cell{padding:0;background:var(--paper);position:relative;overflow:hidden;}
.showcase-embed-cell .showcase-frame-wrap{position:relative;width:100%;height:100%;overflow:hidden;background:var(--paper);}
.showcase-embed-cell iframe{
  position:absolute;top:0;left:0;width:1440px;height:900px;border:0;background:var(--paper);
  transform-origin:top left;pointer-events:none;
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  .showcase-embed-cell{position:sticky;top:48px;height:56svh;z-index:2;}
}
@media (min-width:768px){
  /* R6 §3, two stacked causes, both fixed here:
     1) .showcase-side's natural content (all 5/6 rows, R5's rise-mask kept
        every body visible at once) was taller than the embed cell's
        explicit height. A CSS grid item with an explicit height does not
        stretch to match a taller sibling's row track - the TRACK grows to
        fit the tall side instead, leaving the embed cell short of the
        row's actual height by the difference (measured ~110px), exposing
        the stage's own black gap background below the frame. Pinning both
        columns to the SAME explicit height (with the side's own
        overflow-y:auto as a never-clip safety net) makes them structurally
        impossible to mismatch, regardless of how much text a future edit
        adds.
     2) That explicit height was `100svh - 48px`, sized to sit BELOW the
        48px sticky topline - but the pin (`start:'top top'`) puts the
        section's rendered top at the viewport's own y:0, with the topline
        merely painted on top of (not offsetting) its first 48px. The
        result: content correctly avoids the topline visually, but then
        runs 48px short of the viewport's bottom edge, showing the stage's
        black background as a trailing band under both columns (measured:
        embed/side bottom at 852 of a 900-tall viewport). Hero's own pin
        has this identical 48px arithmetic and gap - invisible there only
        because it lands on the page's own black background either side.
        Showcase's is visible because there's real content flush above it.
        Fixed the same way hero's is invisible: fill the FULL viewport
        (100svh) - the topline still visually covers the top 48px (it's
        position:sticky, z-index:40, opaque), but the bottom now lands
        exactly on the viewport edge, so no gap is left to expose. */
  .showcase-embed-cell{height:100svh;}
  .showcase-side{height:100svh;overflow-y:auto;}
}
.showcase-side{display:grid;grid-template-rows:auto 1fr;gap:1px;background:#000;}
.showcase-panel{display:contents;}
.showcase-head{padding:calc(var(--cellpad)*1.4) var(--cellpad);}
.showcase-head .headline-40{margin-bottom:8px;}
.showcase-rows{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:1px;background:#000;}

/* R6 §1/§2: replaced the "every row's full body always in the DOM,
   rise-mask reveal" layout (which had no height limit and let row 2's
   body run past its cell's bottom - real, measured clipping, not a near
   miss) with a scroll-driven ledger: every row always shows its heading;
   only the ACTIVE row expands its body via a height reveal. Collapsed rows
   can never overflow because they have no body box to overflow - this is
   what actually guarantees "no text may ever be clipped", not a taller
   cell. Desktop/tablet only (see the max-width:767px override below) -
   mobile keeps every body visible, per spec. */
/* flex:1 (not just auto height) so the five/six rows always share the
   FULL height of the ledger column between them - without it the rows'
   own natural (mostly collapsed) height left empty space at the bottom of
   the column, showing the flex container's own black gap background
   (a smaller instance of the same "dead band" defect as R6 §6). */
/* R6 bugfix: `min-height:0` let flex:1 SHRINK a row below its own content
   (needed to grow rows into leftover space, but it also let the browser
   squeeze a merely-taller-by-a-few-px collapsed heading below its natural
   line height when six rows shared a shorter 800px column - measured
   2-19px of real overflow on Hoerai's rows at 1280x800). Leaving min-height
   at its flex default (auto = content size) means a row can grow but never
   shrink below what its own heading needs; any genuine total shortfall
   falls through to .showcase-side's own overflow-y:auto (a scrollbar,
   never silent clipping). */
.showcase-row{padding:var(--cellpad);flex:1;display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:center;}
.showcase-row h3{margin-bottom:0;transition:opacity .3s ease;}
.showcase-row.is-upcoming h3{opacity:.6;} /* lead R6: .35 gav ~2:1 mot svart och grått; .6 ger ≥3,7:1 (stor text, AA 3:1) */
.showcase-row.is-active h3,.showcase-row.is-past h3{opacity:1;}
@media (min-width:768px){
  .showcase-row .row-body{
    display:grid;grid-template-rows:0fr;
    transition:grid-template-rows .45s cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1);
  }
  .showcase-row.is-active .row-body{grid-template-rows:1fr;}
  .showcase-row .row-body-inner{overflow:hidden;min-height:0;}
  .showcase-row .row-body-inner p{margin-top:8px;}
}
.showcase-row p{max-width:52ch;font-size:15px;}
@media (max-width:767px){
  /* mobile: no accordion (spec) - every body stays visible, stacked. */
  .showcase-row .row-body-inner p{margin-top:8px;}
}
.showcase-panel--calyx .showcase-row:nth-child(odd){background:var(--paper);}
.showcase-panel--calyx .showcase-row:nth-child(even){background:var(--grey);}
.showcase-panel--horai .showcase-row:nth-child(odd){background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);}
.showcase-panel--horai .showcase-row:nth-child(odd) p{color:#bdbdbd;}
.showcase-panel--horai .showcase-row:nth-child(even){background:var(--grey);}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- pris */
.pris-statement{padding:calc(var(--cellpad)*2) var(--cellpad);}
.pris-statement .body-30{max-width:60ch;margin-top:16px;font-weight:500;}
/* All placement lives in these classes (not inline styles) so the media
   queries below can actually win the cascade at each breakpoint. */
.pris-bento{grid-template-columns:repeat(12,1fr);grid-template-rows:auto auto;}
.pris-lead{grid-column:1 / span 6;grid-row:1 / span 2;background:var(--mint);display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:space-between;gap:24px;}
.pris-tier{display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:space-between;gap:18px;min-height:220px;}
.pris-tier-a{grid-column:7 / span 6;grid-row:1;background:var(--paper);}
.pris-tier-b{grid-column:7 / span 6;grid-row:2;background:var(--grey);}
@media (max-width:1199px){
  .pris-bento{grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;}
  .pris-lead{grid-column:1 / span 2;grid-row:1;}
  .pris-tier-a{grid-column:1;grid-row:2;}
  .pris-tier-b{grid-column:2;grid-row:2;}
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  .pris-bento{grid-template-columns:1fr;}
  .pris-lead,.pris-tier-a,.pris-tier-b{grid-column:1;grid-row:auto;min-height:0;}
}
.price-label{max-width:34ch;font-size:15px;}
.price-value{font-size:clamp(28px,3.6vw,44px);letter-spacing:-.03em;}
.price-value .unit{font-size:.5em;margin-left:2px;}
.price-value--text{font-size:clamp(18px,2vw,24px);}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- kontakt (R5 §C: heron speglad) */
.kontakt-quad{
  position:relative;display:grid;gap:1px;background:#000;min-height:100svh;
  grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;grid-template-rows:1fr 1fr;
  grid-template-areas:"ov oh" "nv nh";
}
.kontakt-q{position:relative;overflow:hidden;padding:var(--cellpad);}
.kontakt-q--ov{grid-area:ov;background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:flex-end;gap:10px;}
/* R6 §4: headline-40 is tuned for a single "jätteord" (hero, case names) -
   at this cell's half-page width, a four-word sentence in it ran past the
   ÖV/ÖH seam (measured x>720 at 1440, into the card's own space). A
   smaller, dedicated clamp - same family as the old kontakt-giant's - fits
   three lines comfortably inside the cell at 1440/1280/768, verified with
   getBoundingClientRect against the cell box, not eyeballed. */
.kontakt-q--ov h2{
  font-size:clamp(1.75rem, 1.1rem + 2.6vw, 3.4rem);line-height:1.05;
  letter-spacing:-.03em;font-weight:500;max-width:12ch;
}
.kontakt-q--ov p{max-width:32ch;font-size:15px;}
.kontakt-q--oh{grid-area:oh;background:var(--paper);}
.kontakt-q--nv{grid-area:nv;background:var(--grey);padding:0;}
.kontakt-q--nh{grid-area:nh;background:var(--mint);}
@media (max-width:767px){
  /* R6 §7: nh gets more room than ov/nv (was the same minmax(60vw) as
     both) - a 3D Y-axis rotation's perspective projection genuinely bulges
     a flat card's rendered bounding box taller at the near edge as it
     turns (measured: +/-28px top/bottom at 1200px perspective, still
     +/-24px at 3000px - foreshortening a rotated rectangle really does
     grow its axis-aligned bbox, not a rounding artefact), and centring an
     88%-wide card in a 60vw-tall row left only ~27px clearance to the
     subline above - not enough to survive that bulge at any angle in the
     0-180deg sweep. */
  .kontakt-quad{grid-template-columns:1fr;grid-template-rows:minmax(60vw,auto) minmax(76vw,auto) minmax(60vw,auto);grid-template-areas:"ov" "nh" "nv";min-height:auto;}
  .kontakt-q--oh{display:none;}
}

/* the card sits on the crossing of all four quadrants (a grid item that
   spans the full 2x2 and centres itself), mirroring heron's own card. On
   mobile it drops into the mint cell's own grid area instead, 88% wide. */
/* R6 §4/§7: centred on the FULL 2x2 crossing put the card's top edge only
   ~15-50px below the headline row at rest, with zero margin for the flip's
   lift or the hover-tilt's foreshortening - both could (and did, measured)
   bring the card within single-digit px of "verksamhet.". Spanning only
   the LOWER row (grid-row:2, still centred horizontally on the vertical
   seam = still "on the crossing") puts the card inside the NV/NH half
   entirely, with a full row-height of clearance above it before ÖV even
   starts. */
.kontakt-card-anchor{
  grid-column:1 / 3;grid-row:2;place-self:center;z-index:5;
  width:min(32vw,460px);aspect-ratio:85/55;perspective:1200px;
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  .kontakt-card-anchor{grid-area:nh;place-self:center;width:80%;}
}
.kontakt-card-tilt{width:100%;height:100%;position:relative;transform-style:preserve-3d;}
.card-flip2{width:100%;height:100%;position:relative;transform-style:preserve-3d;box-shadow:10px 10px 0 0 #000;}
.card-flip2 button.face{margin:0;padding:6%;font:inherit;text-align:left;cursor:pointer;display:block;width:100%;height:100%;}
.card-flip2 button.face:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--mint);outline-offset:2px;}
.face-back-hit{position:absolute;inset:0;z-index:0;background:transparent;border:0;padding:0;margin:0;cursor:pointer;}
.face-back-hit:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--mint);outline-offset:2px;}
.card-back-content{position:relative;z-index:1;height:100%;display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:center;gap:10px;pointer-events:none;}
.card-back-content a{pointer-events:auto;}
.card-back-links{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;margin-top:4px;}
.card-back-links a{font-size:clamp(13px,1.5vw,18px);text-decoration:underline;width:max-content;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- footer */
.footer-cell{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);padding:0 0 0 var(--cellpad);height:34vw;max-height:340px;min-height:200px;display:flex;align-items:flex-end;overflow:hidden;}
.footer-mark{font-size:clamp(80px,16vw,220px);line-height:.8;letter-spacing:-.04em;white-space:nowrap;padding-bottom:.06em;}
.footer-strip{padding:18px var(--cellpad);background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);}
.footer-strip a{text-decoration:underline;font-size:14px;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- resolve (dither -> color) */
.img-cell{position:relative;}
/* R3: §3 dither -> colour grid-stagger. The tile grid sits over the
   already-visible colour layer; each tile shows one slice of the dither
   image and fades on its own random-order schedule, so the resolve reads
   as pixels dissolving away rather than a wipe. Built once at init from
   the existing .dither-layer <img> (see buildTileGrid in the script). */
.tile-grid{position:absolute;inset:0;display:grid;pointer-events:none;}
.tile-grid > span{display:block;background-repeat:no-repeat;will-change:opacity;}
.color-layer{clip-path:none;}

/* R3: seam-anchored decorations, all created/positioned by the script. */
.seam-line{position:absolute;background:var(--mint);pointer-events:none;z-index:3;}
/* the crosshair seam-draw is a 2x2-grid flourish; hero-stage stacks to one
   column under 768px (see .hero-stage media query above), so the same
   absolute-positioned lines would otherwise bisect the whole stacked
   column top to bottom - hide them there. */
@media (max-width:767px){ .seam-line{display:none;} }
.process-row{position:relative;}
.process-progress{position:absolute;top:0;bottom:0;width:2px;background:var(--mint);transform:scaleY(0);transform-origin:top center;pointer-events:none;z-index:6;}
/* process-left/process-right only sit side by side at the 1200px+ 12-col
   grid (BYGGSPEC .g12 breakpoints); below that they stack, so the seam
   the progress line marks no longer exists - hide it rather than let a
   stale left-offset poke 2px past the right edge (390/768 overflow). */
@media (max-width:1199px){ .process-progress{display:none;} }

/* R3: SplitText's own mask:'lines'/'words'/'chars' option wraps each split
   unit in its own clipping span, and every heading that gets split already
   sits inside a .cell (overflow:hidden) or .footer-cell (overflow:hidden)
   — so no extra clip rule is needed on the headings themselves (adding one
   risked cutting descenders that round 2's static layout already relies
   on fitting without it). */

/* spacing rhythm between section groups */
.rhythm{height:110px;}
@media (max-width:767px){ .rhythm{height:72px;} }
</style>
</head>

<script>
(function(){
  'use strict';
  gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger, SplitText);

  /* ============================================================ §0 motorn
     Lenis <-> GSAP wiring per lenis-skillen, ordagrant: autoRaf:false,
     gsap.ticker som enda RAF-drivare, lagSmoothing(0), scroll -> ST.update.
     respectReducedMotion:false: rörelse spelar alltid (F-011, spec §0). ----- */
  var lenis = new Lenis({ autoRaf: false, anchors: true, respectReducedMotion: false, lerp: 0.1 });
  window.__lenis = lenis; /* dev hook: lets §10's jump-test drive lenis.scrollTo(...,{immediate:true}) */
  gsap.ticker.add(function(time){ lenis.raf(time * 1000); });
  gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0);
  lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update);

  /* R5 fix: a ScrollTrigger.refresh() that lands WHILE the calyx showcase
     iframe is still navigating (its 'load' hasn't fired yet - a live
     same-origin document loading INSIDE an already-pinned element) reliably
     threw "insertBefore ... no longer a child" from ScrollTrigger's own
     pin-revert step, reproduced by bisecting away pin/scrub/onRefresh/the
     iframe itself one at a time until only "pin + a loading iframe inside
     it" remained. fonts.ready, every not-yet-loaded <img>'s load event, and
     the two setTimeout sweeps below can all land in that same early window,
     so every refresh() in the file is routed through this one gate: it
     queues (never drops) until the showcase iframe has fully settled, then
     also coalesces same-frame calls into one trailing refresh(). */
  var __showcaseIframeSettled = false;
  var __refreshTimer = null;
  function safeRefresh(){
    if (!__showcaseIframeSettled){
      if (__refreshTimer) clearTimeout(__refreshTimer);
      __refreshTimer = setTimeout(safeRefresh, 60);
      return;
    }
    if (__refreshTimer) clearTimeout(__refreshTimer);
    __refreshTimer = setTimeout(function(){ __refreshTimer = null; ScrollTrigger.refresh(); }, 200);
  }

  /* ----- lazy iframe mount, same sweep principle as V3e, now driven by the
     Lenis scroll event instead of a native scroll listener so it keeps
     firing during smoothed scroll, on anchors, and on a straight jump. ----- */
  var frames = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('iframe[data-src]'));
  var AHEAD = 2;
  var defer = window.requestIdleCallback
    ? function(fn){ requestIdleCallback(fn, { timeout: 600 }); }
    : function(fn){ setTimeout(fn, 1); };
  function mountFrame(f){
    var src = f.getAttribute('data-src');
    if (!src) return;
    f.addEventListener('load', function(){ safeRefresh(); }, { once: true });
    f.src = src;
    f.removeAttribute('data-src');
  }
  function mountDue(){
    if (!frames.length) return;
    var edge = window.innerHeight * AHEAD;
    for (var i = frames.length - 1; i >= 0; i--){
      if (frames[i].getBoundingClientRect().top < edge){
        (function(f){ defer(function(){ mountFrame(f); }); })(frames[i]);
        frames.splice(i, 1);
      }
    }

  lenis.on('scroll', mountDue);
  addEventListener('load', mountDue);

  Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('img')).forEach(function(img){

  /* ============================================================ §3 dither -> färg
     GSAP grid-stagger (cyphr-studio lån, byggspec §1): each image cell
     gets a tile grid of <span>s cut from the dither image, layered over
     the now fully-visible colour layer. Tiles fade out on a random-order
     schedule scrubbed to the cell's own scroll range, so the resolve reads
     as pixels dissolving away, reversible on scroll-back. Hero cells
     (data-resolve="stay") keep their flat dither look and are excluded,
     per spec §3 ("alla bildceller utom heron"). ----- */
  function buildTileGrid(cell, rows, cols){
    var dither = cell.querySelector('.dither-layer');
    var color = cell.querySelector('.color-layer');
    if (!dither || !color) return null;
    gsap.set(color, { clipPath: 'inset(0px 0px 0px 0px)' });
    var src = dither.getAttribute('src');
    var grid = document.createElement('div');
    grid.className = 'tile-grid';
    grid.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
    grid.style.gridTemplateColumns = 'repeat(' + cols + ',1fr)';
    grid.style.gridTemplateRows = 'repeat(' + rows + ',1fr)';

    for (var r = 0; r < rows; r++){

        var t = document.createElement('span');
        t.style.backgroundImage = 'url(' + src + ')';
        t.style.backgroundSize = (cols * 100) + '% ' + (rows * 100) + '%';
        t.style.backgroundPosition = (cols < 2 ? 0 : (c / (cols - 1) * 100)) + '% ' + (rows < 2 ? 0 : (r / (rows - 1) * 100)) + '%';
        frag.appendChild(t);
        tiles.push(t);
      }

    cell.appendChild(grid);

        fit the tall side instead, leaving the embed cell short of the
        row's actual height by the difference (measured ~110px), exposing
        the stage's own black gap background below the frame. Pinning both
        columns to the SAME explicit height (with the side's own
        overflow-y:auto as a never-clip safety net) makes them structurally
        impossible to mismatch, regardless of how much text a future edit
        adds.
     2) That explicit height was `100svh - 48px`, sized to sit BELOW the
        48px sticky topline - but the pin (`start:'top top'`) puts the
        section's rendered top at the viewport's own y:0, with the topline
        merely painted on top of (not offsetting) its first 48px. The
        result: content correctly avoids the topline visually, but then
        runs 48px short of the viewport's bottom edge, showing the stage's
        black background as a trailing band under both columns (measured:
        embed/side bottom at 852 of a 900-tall viewport). Hero's own pin
        has this identical 48px arithmetic and gap - invisible there only
        because it lands on the page's own black background either side.
        Showcase's is visible because there's real content flush above it.
        Fixed the same way hero's is invisible: fill the FULL viewport
        (100svh) - the topline still visually covers the top 48px (it's
        position:sticky, z-index:40, opaque), but the bottom now lands
        exactly on the viewport edge, so no gap is left to expose. */
  .showcase-embed-cell{height:100svh;}
  .showcase-side{height:100svh;overflow-y:auto;}
}
.showcase-side{display:grid;grid-template-rows:auto 1fr;gap:1px;background:#000;}
.showcase-panel{display:contents;}
.showcase-head{padding:calc(var(--cellpad)*1.4) var(--cellpad);}
.showcase-head .headline-40{margin-bottom:8px;}
.showcase-rows{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:1px;background:#000;}

/* R6 §1/§2: replaced the "every row's full body always in the DOM,
   rise-mask reveal" layout (which had no height limit and let row 2's
   body run past its cell's bottom - real, measured clipping, not a near
   miss) with a scroll-driven ledger: every row always shows its heading;
   only the ACTIVE row expands its body via a height reveal. Collapsed rows
   can never overflow because they have no body box to overflow - this is
   what actually guarantees "no text may ever be clipped", not a taller
   cell. Desktop/tablet only (see the max-width:767px override below) -
   mobile keeps every body visible, per spec. */
/* flex:1 (not just auto height) so the five/six rows always share the
   FULL height of the ledger column between them - without it the rows'
   own natural (mostly collapsed) height left empty space at the bottom of
   the column, showing the flex container's own black gap background
   (a smaller instance of the same "dead band" defect as R6 §6). */
/* R6 bugfix: `min-height:0` let flex:1 SHRINK a row below its own content
   (needed to grow rows into leftover space, but it also let the browser
   squeeze a merely-taller-by-a-few-px collapsed heading below its natural
   line height when six rows shared a shorter 800px column - measured
   2-19px of real overflow on Hoerai's rows at 1280x800). Leaving min-height
   at its flex default (auto = content size) means a row can grow but never
   shrink below what its own heading needs; any genuine total shortfall
   falls through to .showcase-side's own overflow-y:auto (a scrollbar,
   never silent clipping). */
.showcase-row{padding:var(--cellpad);flex:1;display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:center;}
.showcase-row h3{margin-bottom:0;transition:opacity .3s ease;}
.showcase-row.is-upcoming h3{opacity:.6;} /* lead R6: .35 gav ~2:1 mot svart och grått; .6 ger ≥3,7:1 (stor text, AA 3:1) */
.showcase-row.is-active h3,.showcase-row.is-past h3{opacity:1;}
@media (min-width:768px){
  .showcase-row .row-body{
    display:grid;grid-template-rows:0fr;
    transition:grid-template-rows .45s cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1);
  }
  .showcase-row.is-active .row-body{grid-template-rows:1fr;}
  .showcase-row .row-body-inner{overflow:hidden;min-height:0;}
  .showcase-row .row-body-inner p{margin-top:8px;}
}
.showcase-row p{max-width:52ch;font-size:15px;}
@media (max-width:767px){
  /* mobile: no accordion (spec) - every body stays visible, stacked. */
  .showcase-row .row-body-inner p{margin-top:8px;}
}
.showcase-panel--calyx .showcase-row:nth-child(odd){background:var(--paper);}
.showcase-panel--calyx .showcase-row:nth-child(even){background:var(--grey);}
.showcase-panel--horai .showcase-row:nth-child(odd){background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);}
.showcase-panel--horai .showcase-row:nth-child(odd) p{color:#bdbdbd;}
.showcase-panel--horai .showcase-row:nth-child(even){background:var(--grey);}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- pris */
.pris-statement{padding:calc(var(--cellpad)*2) var(--cellpad);}
.pris-statement .body-30{max-width:60ch;margin-top:16px;font-weight:500;}
/* All placement lives in these classes (not inline styles) so the media
   queries below can actually win the cascade at each breakpoint. */
.pris-bento{grid-template-columns:repeat(12,1fr);grid-template-rows:auto auto;}
.pris-lead{grid-column:1 / span 6;grid-row:1 / span 2;background:var(--mint);display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:space-between;gap:24px;}
.pris-tier{display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:space-between;gap:18px;min-height:220px;}
.pris-tier-a{grid-column:7 / span 6;grid-row:1;background:var(--paper);}
.pris-tier-b{grid-column:7 / span 6;grid-row:2;background:var(--grey);}
@media (max-width:1199px){
  .pris-bento{grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;}
  .pris-lead{grid-column:1 / span 2;grid-row:1;}
  .pris-tier-a{grid-column:1;grid-row:2;}
  .pris-tier-b{grid-column:2;grid-row:2;}
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  .pris-bento{grid-template-columns:1fr;}
  .pris-lead,.pris-tier-a,.pris-tier-b{grid-column:1;grid-row:auto;min-height:0;}
}
.price-label{max-width:34ch;font-size:15px;}
.price-value{font-size:clamp(28px,3.6vw,44px);letter-spacing:-.03em;}
.price-value .unit{font-size:.5em;margin-left:2px;}
.price-value--text{font-size:clamp(18px,2vw,24px);}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- kontakt (R5 §C: heron speglad) */
.kontakt-quad{
  position:relative;display:grid;gap:1px;background:#000;min-height:100svh;
  grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;grid-template-rows:1fr 1fr;
  grid-template-areas:"ov oh" "nv nh";
}
.kontakt-q{position:relative;overflow:hidden;padding:var(--cellpad);}
.kontakt-q--ov{grid-area:ov;background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:flex-end;gap:10px;}
/* R6 §4: headline-40 is tuned for a single "jätteord" (hero, case names) -
   at this cell's half-page width, a four-word sentence in it ran past the
   ÖV/ÖH seam (measured x>720 at 1440, into the card's own space). A
   smaller, dedicated clamp - same family as the old kontakt-giant's - fits
   three lines comfortably inside the cell at 1440/1280/768, verified with
   getBoundingClientRect against the cell box, not eyeballed. */
.kontakt-q--ov h2{
  font-size:clamp(1.75rem, 1.1rem + 2.6vw, 3.4rem);line-height:1.05;
  letter-spacing:-.03em;font-weight:500;max-width:12ch;
}
.kontakt-q--ov p{max-width:32ch;font-size:15px;}
.kontakt-q--oh{grid-area:oh;background:var(--paper);}
.kontakt-q--nv{grid-area:nv;background:var(--grey);padding:0;}
.kontakt-q--nh{grid-area:nh;background:var(--mint);}
@media (max-width:767px){
  /* R6 §7: nh gets more room than ov/nv (was the same minmax(60vw) as
     both) - a 3D Y-axis rotation's perspective projection genuinely bulges
     a flat card's rendered bounding box taller at the near edge as it
     turns (measured: +/-28px top/bottom at 1200px perspective, still
     +/-24px at 3000px - foreshortening a rotated rectangle really does
     grow its axis-aligned bbox, not a rounding artefact), and centring an
     88%-wide card in a 60vw-tall row left only ~27px clearance to the
     subline above - not enough to survive that bulge at any angle in the
     0-180deg sweep. */
  .kontakt-quad{grid-template-columns:1fr;grid-template-rows:minmax(60vw,auto) minmax(76vw,auto) minmax(60vw,auto);grid-template-areas:"ov" "nh" "nv";min-height:auto;}
  .kontakt-q--oh{display:none;}
}

/* the card sits on the crossing of all four quadrants (a grid item that
   spans the full 2x2 and centres itself), mirroring heron's own card. On
   mobile it drops into the mint cell's own grid area instead, 88% wide. */
/* R6 §4/§7: centred on the FULL 2x2 crossing put the card's top edge only
   ~15-50px below the headline row at rest, with zero margin for the flip's
   lift or the hover-tilt's foreshortening - both could (and did, measured)
   bring the card within single-digit px of "verksamhet.". Spanning only
   the LOWER row (grid-row:2, still centred horizontally on the vertical
   seam = still "on the crossing") puts the card inside the NV/NH half
   entirely, with a full row-height of clearance above it before ÖV even
   starts. */
.kontakt-card-anchor{
  grid-column:1 / 3;grid-row:2;place-self:center;z-index:5;
  width:min(32vw,460px);aspect-ratio:85/55;perspective:1200px;
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  .kontakt-card-anchor{grid-area:nh;place-self:center;width:80%;}
}
.kontakt-card-tilt{width:100%;height:100%;position:relative;transform-style:preserve-3d;}
.card-flip2{width:100%;height:100%;position:relative;transform-style:preserve-3d;box-shadow:10px 10px 0 0 #000;}
.card-flip2 button.face{margin:0;padding:6%;font:inherit;text-align:left;cursor:pointer;display:block;width:100%;height:100%;}
.card-flip2 button.face:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--mint);outline-offset:2px;}
.face-back-hit{position:absolute;inset:0;z-index:0;background:transparent;border:0;padding:0;margin:0;cursor:pointer;}
.face-back-hit:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--mint);outline-offset:2px;}
.card-back-content{position:relative;z-index:1;height:100%;display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:center;gap:10px;pointer-events:none;}
.card-back-content a{pointer-events:auto;}
.card-back-links{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;margin-top:4px;}
.card-back-links a{font-size:clamp(13px,1.5vw,18px);text-decoration:underline;width:max-content;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- footer */
.footer-cell{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);padding:0 0 0 var(--cellpad);height:34vw;max-height:340px;min-height:200px;display:flex;align-items:flex-end;overflow:hidden;}
.footer-mark{font-size:clamp(80px,16vw,220px);line-height:.8;letter-spacing:-.04em;white-space:nowrap;padding-bottom:.06em;}
.footer-strip{padding:18px var(--cellpad);background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);}
.footer-strip a{text-decoration:underline;font-size:14px;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- resolve (dither -> color) */
.img-cell{position:relative;}
/* R3: §3 dither -> colour grid-stagger. The tile grid sits over the
   already-visible colour layer; each tile shows one slice of the dither
   image and fades on its own random-order schedule, so the resolve reads
   as pixels dissolving away rather than a wipe. Built once at init from
   the existing .dither-layer <img> (see buildTileGrid in the script). */
.tile-grid{position:absolute;inset:0;display:grid;pointer-events:none;}
.tile-grid > span{display:block;background-repeat:no-repeat;will-change:opacity;}
.color-layer{clip-path:none;}

/* R3: seam-anchored decorations, all created/positioned by the script. */
.seam-line{position:absolute;background:var(--mint);pointer-events:none;z-index:3;}
/* the crosshair seam-draw is a 2x2-grid flourish; hero-stage stacks to one
   column under 768px (see .hero-stage media query above), so the same
   absolute-positioned lines would otherwise bisect the whole stacked
   column top to bottom - hide them there. */
@media (max-width:767px){ .seam-line{display:none;} }
.process-row{position:relative;}
.process-progress{position:absolute;top:0;bottom:0;width:2px;background:var(--mint);transform:scaleY(0);transform-origin:top center;pointer-events:none;z-index:6;}
/* process-left/process-right only sit side by side at the 1200px+ 12-col
   grid (BYGGSPEC .g12 breakpoints); below that they stack, so the seam
   the progress line marks no longer exists - hide it rather than let a
   stale left-offset poke 2px past the right edge (390/768 overflow). */
@media (max-width:1199px){ .process-progress{display:none;} }

/* R3: SplitText's own mask:'lines'/'words'/'chars' option wraps each split
   unit in its own clipping span, and every heading that gets split already
   sits inside a .cell (overflow:hidden) or .footer-cell (overflow:hidden)
   — so no extra clip rule is needed on the headings themselves (adding one
   risked cutting descenders that round 2's static layout already relies
   on fitting without it). */

/* spacing rhythm between section groups */
.rhythm{height:110px;}
@media (max-width:767px){ .rhythm{height:72px;} }
</style>
</head>
